docs.title: Evaluate the prototype
docs.text: This experiment tests whether a small, edited operator guide is useful before committing to a full manual migration.

docs.title: Try these tasks
docs.text:
1. Find the instructions appropriate to your installed version.
  2. Find how to reopen an existing contest.
  3. Switch between serial and network radio instructions.
  4. Search for WSJT-X BROADCAST PORT and follow the result to the setup procedure.
  5. Switch to dark mode and review a table on a narrow screen.
  6. Open the built site locally with the network disconnected and check search and navigation.
  7. Find how to set a backup interval and identify the manual backup key.
  8. Find how to log two worked parks and check the resulting ADIF fields.
  9. Find the distinction between TR4W's name and the availability of a particular native build.

Record whether each task succeeds without help, where you hesitate, and any label that differs from the actual program. These are evaluation tasks, not claimed test results.

docs.title: What Material contributes
docs.text: The prototype uses navigation sections, browser-side search, light/dark themes, tabbed procedures, expandable evidence notes, and offline support. Fonts use the local system stack. No custom theme or external JavaScript service is required.

docs.title: What still requires editorial work
docs.text: MkDocs turns reviewed Markdown into a navigable site. It does not resolve conflicting manuals or determine whether a feature works. The main ongoing effort will be verifying procedures and maintaining their relationship to releases.

docs.title: Suggested next slice
docs.text:
Complete one first-QSO walkthrough with screenshots, then run the drafted backup/export, POTA, and keyboard procedures with an operator on the target platform. Follow with CW setup and a tested migration/recovery walkthrough. A generated settings index could follow once defaults, scope, and help text have a reliable extraction contract.

Reviewed updates are published to the public GitHub Pages preview.

docs.title: Editorial rules
docs.text:
The operating additions also reconcile the old reference manual and wiki SO2R tips with current code: colors and resizing (uPrefsForm, uMainForm), monitor recovery (MainUnit, uWindowLayoutStore), radio-panel fields (uRadioPanelForm), callsign assistance (logedit, logscp), message programming (uEditMessageForm, logsend), HamScore (uHamScore, Tools and status-window handlers), and radio reconnects (ResetRadioPorts). Each page records its source check. Physical-radio, multi-monitor, remote-scoreboard, and GUI restore rehearsals remain open.

The earlier HamScore status-window resync limitation has been fixed in the reviewed source. Both entry points now use a confirmation dialog offering re-send only, delete and re-send, or cancel; the operator page reflects that behavior.

  1. Label the target version and platform. Never turn a development plan into a released feature claim.
  2. Start a procedure with an operator task and finish with a visible success check.
  3. Verify field names and defaults in current forms and code; verify behavior by running the procedure.
  4. Keep earlier-version reference material distinguishable from current instructions.
  5. Record the source revision when reviewing a page. Update the documentation with the corresponding code change.
  6. Keep TR4W as the product name. Lead with cross-platform contest logging and TRLOG heritage; keep the historical Windows expansion out of prominent product copy. Qualify native platform availability by release.

docs.title: Gaps this experiment exposed
docs.text:
• This version runs natively on Windows, macOS, and Linux; project-owner clarification confirms macOS operation. Older public copy must not obscure that platform support.
  • The wiki's INI-oriented setup needs reconciliation with the current settings store.
  • The local keyboard inventory dates from April 2026. The selected keyboard page now uses the current accelerator table; a full context-sensitive key audit remains open.
  • Proposal files such as NETWORK_LOG_AUTO_SYNC.md describe intended changes, not proof of implemented behavior.
  • Backup and export now have source-checked procedures. Hands-on migration, backup, recovery, and export checks remain open.
  • Language review policy changed after the translator guide: this testing build includes fuzzy UI text unless built with -ReviewedOnly.
  • Current path code places native Unix contest files in ~/tr4w; the older Linux installation paragraph locating them beside the binary is stale.

docs.title: About TR4W
docs.text:
TR4W — Cross-platform contest logging, rooted in TRLOG.

TR4W is the product name. It carries the history and recognition of a contest logger descended from N6TR's TRLOG as development expands across desktop platforms.

docs.title: A familiar name with a longer history
docs.text:
TR4W began as TRLOG for Windows, derived from the DOS-era contest logger created by Larry “Tree” Tyree, N6TR. That history explains the name; it does not limit the application's future to Windows.

TR4W and TRLinux are separate projects. TRLinux is an independent Linux port of the original TRLOG; a native Linux build of TR4W belongs to the TR4W development line.

docs.title: One product across platforms
docs.text:
Use TR4W for Windows, TR4W for macOS, and TR4W for Linux when identifying platform-specific builds. The product name stays TR4W.

TR4W runs natively on Windows, macOS, and Linux. This guide documents a development preview; individual hardware features and release readiness still need platform-specific validation. Choose your version identifies the documented snapshot.

docs.title: Native applications
docs.text: The FreePascal/Lazarus application uses native builds for each desktop platform. Install the package for your operating system and follow its hardware and file-location notes.

docs.title: For documentation contributors
docs.text:
Lead with TR4W, its operating purpose, and its TRLOG heritage. Reserve “TRLOG for Windows” for history. State native platform support clearly and describe any feature-specific limitations where they matter.

This page follows the project's positioning direction supplied for this documentation experiment. Historical project context is available in the TR4W repository.

docs.title: Back up your log
docs.text: TR4W creates a verified snapshot of the open contest database. A manual backup works without an external backup destination.

docs.title: Make and check a backup
docs.text:
1. Press Alt+F to back up the open log.
  2. Read the result and note the local snapshot path. Local backups are kept in the backup folder under TR4W's writable settings folder.
  3. If you configured BACKUP DESTINATION, TR4W also copies the snapshot there in the background. Check that copy's completion separately: a successful local snapshot does not prove the external copy completed.
  4. Confirm the reported file exists. Keep a copy on another physical disk for protection against loss of the local disk.

docs.title: Set an automatic interval
docs.text:
Open Ctrl+J → Backup. Set Back up every to the number of new QSOs between backups. 0 disables the automatic schedule.

The interval counts newly logged records since the last successful backup. It starts at zero each session. Dupes, X-QSOs, and contacts received from peers count. Notes are excluded. With automatic backups enabled, the next QSO also triggers a backup if the last successful snapshot is at least 30 minutes old or missing. The snapshot runs in the background. A failure keeps the count and delays the next automatic attempt for five minutes.

Use Copy to (the BACKUP DESTINATION setting) to add a background copy.

docs.title: Snapshot files
docs.text:
The periodic snapshot is named for its log, with periodic.db in the filename. A successful replacement retains the prior snapshot as .bak. A .new file is a staging file: preserve it after a failure, but check the result and diagnostic log before trusting it.

Clear Log first makes a separate UTC-dated snapshot in the local backup folder. If that snapshot fails, clearing stops without removing the contacts. Keep the dated snapshot until you have verified the intended result.

Opening a database with an older schema takes a verified snapshot before conversion. Look for a file named <log> before schema <old> to <new>.db in the local backup folder. TR4W refuses to upgrade the log if it cannot publish the backup. Keep this copy if you may need to return to the older TR4W version.

docs.title: Recover safely
docs.text:
Use TR4W's backup command while the log is open. Copying only an active database file can miss committed contacts still in its write-ahead log.

For a full station archive, close TR4W and retain the contest folder, settings, and custom support files as well. A log snapshot does not back up every station file or credential.

Follow Restore files and recover a contest to rehearse recovery on a separate copy. Check identity, contact count, recent QSOs, and score before relying on it.

Source and review boundary

Reviewed for 5.1.0 against uAppPaths, uLogStore, uLogBackup, uBackupCopyService, and the backup callers. The procedures were reviewed in source.

docs.title: Diagnostic logging: INFO, DEBUG, and TRACE
docs.text: tr4w.log is the diagnostic log, not the SQLite contest database or a Cabrillo submission. Changing its verbosity changes the detail recorded about program activity; it does not change the number of contacts saved.

docs.title: Change the log level
docs.text:
1. Open Preferences with Ctrl+J and select Logging.
  2. Choose the required Log level:.
  3. Apply/save the change. The running logger updates without a restart. Merely selecting a value marks the form as changed; canceling it does not apply that selection.
  4. Reproduce the issue and note its time and the steps you took.
  5. Use Open log file on the same panel to open the active file. Return the level to INFO after gathering the needed detail.
Level Intended use NONE Disable ordinary diagnostic output. FATAL Only the most severe failures. ERROR Errors and more severe messages. WARN Warnings, errors, and fatal messages. INFO Normal operating information; the panel's recommended everyday level. DEBUG More diagnostic detail for investigating a problem. TRACE The most detailed tracing; can produce a much larger file.

The current setting name is DEBUG LOG LEVEL. Despite its name, its allowed values include all seven levels above.

docs.title: Log size and retention
docs.text:
tr4w.log now appends without automatic rotation or the former 10 MB limit. Check available space during long diagnostic sessions. TRACE can produce roughly 100 MB per hour, depending on activity. Close TR4W before archiving or removing an old diagnostic log; preserve the relevant session before starting another capture.

Networked-Icom packet-by-packet output is now TRACE. DEBUG retains connection lifecycle events and session renewal, making it the more useful first choice for connection problems.

docs.title: Trace a particular subsystem
docs.text:
The Logging panel also provides separate controls:

Control Purpose DX cluster — log all telnet traffic More detail about cluster traffic. TCI server — log every command, both directions Trace server-side TCI exchanges. HamLib — debug logging Hamlib-related diagnostics. HamLib — internal trace to hamlib_trace.log Write a separate detailed Hamlib trace. HamLib — async callbacks only, no heartbeat (testing) A test mode that changes behavior; it is not simply another verbosity level.

The form says the three Hamlib settings take effect on the next TR4W start. This differs from the main log level, which takes effect when applied without restarting. Turn on the detail appropriate to the problem rather than selecting every test option.

docs.title: Where diagnostic files go
docs.text:
Platform Default main diagnostic log Windows %APPDATA%\TR4W\tr4w.log for a Program Files install or read-only working folder. Otherwise tr4w.log in the working folder. macOS ~/Library/Logs/TR4W/tr4w.log Linux ~/.local/state/tr4w/tr4w.log, or under the configured XDG state root

The Hamlib trace uses the same diagnostic-log root with filename hamlib_trace.log. The panel's active path and Open log file command are useful when several installations or launch profiles exist. Files and folders shows directory trees, contest databases, and reference-data locations.

Startup records the active data paths, redirection and database journal settings. DEBUG lines tagged [Lookup] identify the source of a callsign lookup's name, QTH, or exchange. Use those lines to distinguish a recent log entry from call history or reference data.

For a useful diagnostic report, retain the relevant log together with the TR4W version, platform, radio or integration involved, reproduction steps, and approximate time. The Logging panel also offers Warn when the log file grows unexpectedly; this is a warning control, not a backup or retention policy.

docs.title: Report a crash
docs.text:
Preserve tr4w.log, including its startup and [CRASH] records, with the version, operating system, approximate time, and actions leading to the failure. Keep the macOS crash report too if the system supplies one. Exception reporting is installed in the application, headless export path, and multi-op server; it cannot guarantee a report after every kind of process or machine failure.

On macOS, raw addresses in a backtrace are expected. The log records the running binary's identity and load address so a developer can decode it afterward. The 5.0.26 release offers separate application and server .dSYM.zip files plus a symbol manifest. Symbols must match the report's UUID, not just its version number. They do not need to be installed inside TR4W.app.

The Windows .dbg is also available separately for matching crash reports. Most operators should send the report and log; download symbols only when helping investigate a failure. These symbol downloads are intended for the alpha/beta testing period.

Source check

Levels: uSettingsModel.pas, LOG_LEVEL_SPELLINGS. UI and apply behavior: ui/lcl/uPrefsForm.lfm and .pas, including SaveLoggingPanel and cbxLogLevelChange. Main log path: uProgramMain.pas. Hamlib trace path: radioFactory/uRadioHamLibDirect.pas. This guide has not exercised the panel in a running application.

docs.title: Export ADIF and Cabrillo
docs.text:
Choose the format required by the receiving program or contest sponsor. Keep the contest database and a backup even after exporting.

For the complete menu inventory, see Reports and exported files. To bring contacts into TR4W, see Import contacts.

Your task Start with Move contacts to another logging application or prepare POTA records ADIF. Prepare a contest submission that requires Cabrillo Cabrillo, with the correct station and category information. Inspect contact data in a spreadsheet The CSV export option.

docs.title: Export ADIF
docs.text:
1. Open the contest you want to export.
  2. Choose File → Export → ADIF.
  3. Review the generated file in the preview. The exporter uses the log's filename with an .ADI extension.
  4. Check representative contacts for callsign, date/time, band, mode, reports, and exchange. For POTA, also check your park and worked-park fields.
  5. Use that file with the receiving application and compare its import report with what you expected to transfer.

The exporter filters records through the program's QSO-validity check. Investigate unexpected omissions rather than assuming every database record must appear in an export. Preserve a separate copy of any export you want to retain before generating a new one at the same path.

docs.title: Export Cabrillo
docs.text:
1. Open the correct contest and choose File → Export → Cabrillo.
  2. Complete and review the station-information window that opens. Check your station callsign, entry category, and contest-specific information.
  3. Confirm the dialog to generate the file, then inspect its header and QSO lines.
  4. Compare the file's exchange and category with the event's submission requirements before submitting it.

You can also open Station information from Tools → Edit Cabrillo Summary... to review the category and station headers before exporting.

Generating a file does not submit it to the sponsor. Retain the submitted file and the sponsor's receipt when you complete that step.

docs.title: Current export details
docs.text:
ADIF, Cabrillo, and CSV files are written beside the contest database using its basename and the appropriate extension. Check the preview path before replacing an earlier export. Station facts saved with individual QSOs are used for their applicable exported station/location fields.

ADIF includes the worked station's DXCC when it writes STATE. JTTY and FT2 use MODE=MFSK with their respective SUBMODE under ADIF 3.1.8. Older TR4W JTTY records remain importable.

ADIF exports a set of linked county-line or rover rows as one contact. For two counties, check USACA_COUNTIES for the worked station and MY_USACA_COUNTIES for your own locations, as applicable. A longer county list uses TR4W extension fields. Check how the receiving application reads those fields. Vermont's separate -ft.adi is written when the log contains contacts assigned to that export.

Hawaii rover logs can produce a Cabrillo file per activation. In an unsplit rover export, the header CALLSIGN is your base call. Inspect the sent call and place on the individual QSO lines. Review CATEGORY-STATION or an overlay where the contest offers one.

docs.title: What to check before delivery
docs.text:
• The file belongs to the intended contest and station.
  • Date/time, frequency or band, mode, and exchanges look right in early and late contacts.
  • Category and station information match your intended entry.
  • A multi-park contact has the expected separate park entries.
  • The receiving application or sponsor accepts the format without unexplained omissions.
Source check

Menu structure: uMenu.pas. Dispatch: MainUnit.pas (menu_adif and menu_cabrillo). ADIF naming, filtering, and preview: ExportToADIF in trdos/postunit.pas. General ADIF fields: uADIF.pas. This draft has not exercised export dialogs or a sponsor's upload service.

docs.title: Import contacts
docs.text: ADIF import adds contacts to the open contest database. Choose the receiving contest before importing; an exchange's interpretation depends on that contest.

docs.title: Import an ADIF file
docs.text:
1. Preserve the original file and back up any receiving contest that already contains contacts.
  2. Create or open the intended contest. For a migration trial, use a separate empty contest.
  3. Choose File → Import → ADIF and select the .adi or .adif file.
  4. If the receiving log is not empty, review the prompt asking whether to append imported QSOs. Cancel if this is not the intended destination.
  5. Review the completion counts and any failures, then check representative calls, dates/times, bands, modes, and exchanges in the log.
  6. Export the resulting contest and compare important fields with the source, especially contest-specific exchanges and multi-location contacts.

The importer collects contacts and writes the batch in one database transaction. A database write failure rolls back that batch, leaving the receiving log unchanged. This does not mean every malformed line is imported: incomplete or malformed input can be skipped and reported. Read the completion counts and skipped-record report, then compare the result with the original file. A successful import rescores and reloads the log.

The import report also names unrecognized CONTEST_ID values. Check those records and the intended contest before exporting or submitting the resulting log.

docs.title: Avoid accidental duplicates
docs.text: The append prompt is not a promise that repeated imports are automatically deduplicated. Keep track of which source files have been imported and check the log before repeating an import. The importer has contest-specific handling, including county-line contacts; unusual repeated calls may be legitimate and need inspection rather than blanket removal.

docs.title: Bringing a 4.x log forward
docs.text:
Export ADIF from the old installation, preserve the original contest folder, and import into a separate correctly selected contest in the new build. The source explicitly supports ADIF import without requiring a .TRW file beside it.

The opening picker also recognizes legacy configurations where no matching database exists, as described in Moving from 4.x. That path should be tested on copies. Neither contact import nor INI-to-JSON conversion by itself proves that all messages, station settings, categories, and contest-specific configuration have migrated.

This guide does not establish a Cabrillo-import command. Cabrillo appears here as an export/submission format.

Source check

MainUnit.pas, ImportFromADIF, supplies the picker, append prompt, batch transaction, skipped-record report, and rescore/reload. uADIF.pas supplies parsing. Tests include uTestLogImport, uTestLogRepository, and ADIF fixtures. No user log was imported for this page.

docs.title: Reports and exported files
docs.text: Use exports to transfer or submit contacts, and reports to inspect the contest. Producing a file is not the same as submitting it.

docs.title: Exports
docs.text:
File → Export choice Use ADIF Transfer contact records to another logger or activity service. Cabrillo Prepare a contest submission where the sponsor requires Cabrillo. CSV Inspect exported data with a spreadsheet or other tabular tool. EDI Export for events/services that require EDI; check the event's requirements. Initial exchanges list Produce exchange-reference output for later use. Notes Export recorded notes.

The ADIF and Cabrillo procedure explains how to generate and inspect those files. Current ADIF, Cabrillo, and CSV exports use the database log's basename with .adi, .log, and .csv, beside that database. Older corpus examples may use different filenames. Inspect the preview and destination rather than assuming every .LOG file is a contest submission.

docs.title: File → Reports
docs.text:
The current menu provides:

  • All callsigns
  • Band changes
  • Continent List
  • First callsign worked in each country
  • First callsign worked in each zone
  • QSOs by country by band
  • Score by hour
  • Summary
  • 3830 Score

Choose a report that answers your operating question: inspect band changes for timing, score by hour for rate, or country-by-band totals for band coverage. The applicable interpretation still depends on the contest.

docs.title: Review before using a report
docs.text:
Confirm the contest and station identity, the relevant band/mode/category, and a few known contacts. After correcting contact data, regenerate the output so you are not reading a stale file. Investigate discrepancies against the stored contacts and contest rules.

A report or claimed score reflects TR4W's interpretation of the log. It does not replace the sponsor's rule checking or adjudication. Retain the actual submitted file and receipt separately.

Evidence and review status

Available names and menu grouping: uMenu.pas and uTR4WStrings.pas. ADIF export: trdos/postunit.pas. Cabrillo corpus contract: tr4w/test/corpus/README.md. This page inventories the current menu; each report's contents and format have not been individually validated in this documentation pass.

docs.title: Restore files and recover a contest
docs.text: The current contest log is a SQLite database. Older instructions for rebuilding or copying a legacy binary log are not the recovery procedure for this version. Ctrl+R, described as “Restore last entry” in the old shortcut list, is an entry-editing action, not database restoration.

docs.title: Resume after a full disk
docs.text:
If TR4W can open the database read-only, you can review the log while writes are blocked. A refused QSO stays in the call and exchange fields and the QSO not saved panel remains visible. Free space on the drive named in the notice, then press Enter to retry the retained entry. Confirm the QSO appears in the log and the writable notice clears the error. On a multi-op station, verify catch-up before continuing.

One Enter saves all linked county-line, multi-park or rover rows in one transaction. A refused save leaves the entry available for retry and sends no contact to the server, external loggers, or UDP. Edit QSO and Alt+Y also keep the edit available when the database refuses it.

docs.title: Correct station facts already logged
docs.text:
Choose Tools → Correct Station Facts… and select the station fact to repair, such as the CQ zone.

Review the affected and skipped row counts before confirming. The confirmation defaults to Cancel. TR4W takes a verified backup, applies the change in one transaction, sends edits to connected systems, and rescores. Imported contacts, rows that never recorded that value, and applicable rover rows are skipped. In Edit QSO, you can inspect or correct individual station facts.

docs.title: Restore a verified log snapshot
docs.text:
1. Stop logging and close TR4W. Preserve the current contest folder before replacing anything, including any .db-wal and .db-shm files that remain. Keep the originals together and untouched for investigation.
  2. Locate the most recent successful TR4W backup. Start with the reported local snapshot in the writable settings folder's backup directory; an optional external destination holds a separate background copy. The snapshot's .bak is the prior snapshot. A .new file needs the backup result/log checked before treating it as a valid backup.
  3. Make a separate working copy of the chosen snapshot in a recovery folder. Give the copy a .db extension if the backup filename has another extension, so it can be selected as a database. Keep the backup itself unchanged.
  4. Start TR4W and open that copy as an existing contest. TR4W performs database identity, version, integrity, and foreign-key checks during opening. If it refuses the file, retain the error and diagnostic log; do not work around it by creating an empty file over the original.
  5. Verify the contest, station identity, contact count, recent QSOs, and score. Determine which QSOs occurred after the snapshot. Reconcile them from independent records before continuing; a successful open alone does not show that the backup contains every contact.
  6. Choose the verified recovered database as the continuing log and set its backup destination appropriately. Keep the original and recovery evidence until reconciliation is complete.

Do not attach old live-database WAL files to a restored snapshot. Use a fresh recovery folder so sidecars from a different database cannot be mixed with it. For a database recovered from a disk rather than a TR4W snapshot, preserve the database and its matching sidecars together and work on copies.

docs.title: Restore settings and reference files
docs.text:
Item Recovery approach tr4w.json station settings and window layout With TR4W closed, retain the current file and restore a known-good copy to the actual settings path. This can restore older radio addresses and window positions; check them before operating. Passwords and API keys stored in the OS credential store are not included in this file; re-enter them when moving to another computer. CTY.DAT and TRMASTER.DTA Restore saved copies or use the reference-data download procedures. Follow the reload/restart instructions. Custom DOM and other contest support files Recover from your station archive. A generic download may not reproduce custom multipliers or local definitions. ADIF/Cabrillo/CSV exports Keep as independent evidence and deliverables. They are not substitutes for a complete database/settings backup. See importing for the supported import route.

The database snapshot does not back up the entire station configuration. See files and folders for platform-specific locations, and window recovery if the problem is only an off-screen window.

Source check and review boundary

Current snapshot behavior: domain/uLogBackup.pas; database opening/validation: uLogStore.pas and uLogDatabase.pas. This is a conservative copy-first recovery procedure derived from those paths. A complete GUI restore rehearsal remains to be performed; no user's log was restored or overwritten while writing this guide.

docs.title: Read the main window
docs.text:
This Florida QSO Party practice log shows TR4W 5.1.0 after one contact on 40 m CW. The contest determines which columns, totals, and exchange details you see.

1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8

Area What to read 1. Totals and score The upper-left table breaks down contacts and multipliers by band. The highlighted heading is the current band. The score is next to the totals. 2. QSO and multiplier needs The upper-right strips show which band and mode combinations still need the displayed station or multiplier, according to the contest rules. Here they refer to W4AFC and Florida. 3. Editable log The center lists saved contacts. The example shows W4AFC on 40 m CW with the received QTH PIN, the points, and the logging operator. 4. Station and timing The lower left shows band and mode, the UTC date and time, radio selection, and CW speed. 5. Next QSO number The large 2 is the next serial TR4W will assign. Contests that exchange a serial can include this number in the sent exchange. 6. Contact entry 599 ALC is the exchange this station sends. Enter the other station's call in the upper white field and its received exchange in the lower field. 7. Operating counters The lower right shows CQ and search-and-pounce contact counts, rate, and operating indicators. 8. Connection status The bottom strip shows messages from Radio 1, Radio 2, DX Cluster, and Network. Open their windows for connection details.

See the radio panels, band map, multiplier windows, and DX Cluster console for their own controls.

docs.title: Set colors
docs.text:
Open Settings → Colors, or Ctrl+J → Appearance → Colors. Each row names a screen element. Choose its foreground (text) and background colors from the offered names; the sample shows the combination as you choose it. Apply or save the preferences to use the colors in the operating windows.

Start with the callsign and exchange fields, editable log, dupe indication, and multiplier indication. Keep text readable against its background. Some status colors deliberately override the normal element color—for example, dupe alerts and the active-radio indication. The Colors page is not a replacement for those status rules. WSJT-X highlighting also uses TR4W's configured dupe and multiplier colors when sending highlights is enabled.

docs.title: Show more QSOs in the main window
docs.text:
Drag the main window wider or taller. The log, possible-call and status areas use the available width, and the main text scales with width. The sent exchange appears above the call field. Set the font and Main window text size in Preferences → Appearance. The earlier ROW COUNT and WINDOW SIZE settings are retired.

SHOW GRIDLINES and NO COLUMN HEADER apply immediately. NO COLUMN HEADER hides the heading row on the log grids and the Network and Stations lists. Hold Alt and drag with the left mouse button to move a tool window whose title bar is hidden by NO CAPTION.

docs.title: Recover a window from a missing monitor
docs.text:
TR4W checks saved positions when opening windows and revalidates open windows after display changes. A window outside the usable displays is moved onto an available monitor. Several recovered windows are staggered so they do not all occupy the same position.

  1. Confirm in the operating system's display settings that the disconnected monitor is no longer part of the desktop. A display that the OS still reports as present can still receive windows.
  2. Restore minimized windows; the live recovery pass skips minimized windows. Open the desired tool window from Windows if it is closed.
  3. If necessary, close and restart TR4W with the current monitor arrangement so saved positions are checked again.
  4. Move the recovered windows where you want them and exit normally to save the layout.

If a monitor returns during the session, an untouched rescued window can return to its original position. Moving it yourself adopts the new position. Layout now lives in the windows section of tr4w.json; old advice to delete tr4w.pos does not reset the current JSON layout. Do not delete the entire settings file to recover one window. See settings locations.

Source check

Earlier manual: “Program Windows — Names and Colors.” Current implementation: uPrefsForm color grid and SaveColorRows, uMainForm resize anchors, MainUnit.EnsureRectOnScreen/RevalidateOpenWindowsOnScreen, and uWindowLayoutStore. Monitor recovery is code-reviewed here, not tested on physical displays.

docs.title: Use the band map
docs.text: The band map organizes spots by operating frequency so you can find stations to work. Its contents depend on incoming spots, age, contest state, and display filters.

docs.title: Find and select a station
docs.text:
Open Band map from the Windows menu. Connect a DX cluster or use another configured spot source. Select a spot to inspect it; double-clicking invokes the tune-to-spot action.

Each row shows a frequency in kHz and a spotted callsign. In this practice feed, the blue selection is N4ZZ on 7020.0 kHz. On the bottom line you can read its age, country and beam heading, and the spotting station. The outline around K1TTT marks the spot nearest the radio's 7025.0 kHz frequency.

In a two-radio setup, double-click behavior can target the inactive radio when the corresponding SO2R setting is enabled and both radios have frequency information. The context menu also offers Send spot to inactive radio. Verify which radio moves before relying on this during a contest.

Tuning to a spot does not complete or log a contact. Confirm the station's callsign and exchange on the air.

docs.title: Worked-multiplier target
docs.text:
Open Ctrl+J → Operating → Band Map → Window and tuning for the Workings of a multiplier before its spot shows no M setting.

BAND MAP WORKED MULT LIMIT accepts 1–9, with 1 as the default. An orange M marks a multiplier already worked fewer times than your chosen target. MULTS ONLY keeps those spots visible. Sweepstakes counts a section across bands and CQ WW counts the relevant multiplier per band.

A spot needs usable multiplier information, such as a section or state in the cluster comment. Tuning to a spot does not count it as worked; logging the contact changes the count.

docs.title: Control what you see
docs.text:
Open Ctrl+J → Operating → Band Map for spot expiry, display limit, and the main filters.

Right-click the map for its display controls:

Control Purpose BAND MAP ALL BANDS Include spots outside the current band. BAND MAP ALL MODES Include other modes. BAND MAP DISPLAY CQ Control display of CQ entries. BAND MAP DUPE DISPLAY Control whether already-worked stations remain visible. BAND MAP MULTS ONLY Limit the view to spots classified as multipliers. BAND MAP SO2R DISPLAY Adjust the two-radio display behavior. Hide digital spots Filter digital spots from the map. Center on radio frequency Center the frequency-ordered view around the radio. Sort by beam heading Sort spots by heading. Centering is unavailable while this sort is active. Text size Enlarge, shrink or reset band-map text independently of the main window. BAND MAP SIZE accepts −4 to 12. Delete selected spot / Remove all spots Remove spot entries, not contacts from the contest log.

BAND MAP DISPLAY LIMIT caps how many spots can display within the available space. The map follows the active radio's band and mode. The nearest spot has an outline, and a spot within the guard band uses the VFO marker color for its frequency. Set the spot, selection and marker colors in Preferences → Appearance → Colors.

Enable BAND MAP CLICK GOES TO EXCHANGE if you want a single click to move keyboard focus to the exchange field. Its default is off.

Spot decay limits how long entries remain useful. BAND MAP DECAY TIME is used as minutes by the display's age calculation. A station can leave the frequency before the spot expires.

docs.title: Why a spot might disappear
docs.text: Check band/mode filters, the mult-only filter, dupe visibility, and age before diagnosing a connection failure. A contact you just logged can change how its spot is classified. Compare the raw cluster console with the filtered map to separate reception from display.

docs.title: How the display stays separate from the data
docs.text:
The spot list owns the spot data; the LCL form owns selection, filtering, and painting. The view requests refreshes through a small interface, with refresh work coalesced by the timer rather than treating every incoming spot as a separate full redraw. This keeps the display and incoming-data processing distinct.

Evidence and review status

Current controls and tuning behavior: ui/lcl/uBandMapForm.lfm and .pas. Data/view boundary: uBandMapView.pas and uSpots.pas. Band-map design history (docs/BANDMAP_LCL_DESIGN.md) supplies rationale but predates the implemented LCL form. Two-radio behavior and colors need a running-build walkthrough.

docs.title: Possible calls and Super Check Partial
docs.text:
Call assistance offers candidates when you copy an incomplete or uncertain callsign. It does not establish what the station actually sent. Confirm the call on the air before logging it.

The older manual distinguishes three related tools:

Tool Purpose and data Partial calls Matches partial input against calls available from the contest's dupe/initial-exchange information. PARTIAL CALL ENABLE controls this feature; WILDCARD PARTIALS controls whether the fragment must start the call. Possible calls Suggests similar calls. POSSIBLE CALLS enables the candidate strip; POSSIBLE CALL MODE controls the candidate source/filter. Super Check Partial (SCP) Searches the master callsign data for a fragment. SCP MINIMUM LETTERS controls automatic activation; SCP COUNTRY STRING restricts the countries included.

Open Ctrl+J → SCP to set the matching threshold, choose countries, or change Possible Call Mode. The current mode defaults to ALL. See the command reference for setting names and accepted values.

docs.title: Contest call history
docs.text:
Enable USE CALL HISTORY FILE and choose CALL HISTORY FILENAME in Preferences to use an N1MM-format history file. For Sweepstakes, a call not already known in the local log can prefill its check and section. With no filename set, the defaults are SSCW.txt for CW and SSSSB.txt for phone. A partial history row can prefill the fields it has. Always confirm the received exchange on the air.

Help → Download call history for this contest downloads supported files on demand, including for Sweepstakes, several other ARRL contests, CWops events, NA Sprint, and many QSO parties. TR4W applies a successful load live. A failed load leaves the previous history in use. If you configured a custom filename, confirm the path in the completion message.

docs.title: Use the possible-call strip
docs.text:
Enter the call or uncertain fragment. Ctrl+P requests possible-call processing (and the associated short-path rotor action if configured). With the default keys, comma selects left, period selects right, and semicolon copies the selected call into the callsign entry field. The three keys are configurable. Selection alone does not log a contact.

The current strip uses bold selection and red/white dupe cells rather than relying on the old manual's angle-bracket cursor illustration. It clears when there are no candidates, so a previous result should not be mistaken for the current search.

docs.title: Maintain the master data
docs.text:
Use Download TRMASTER.DTA and check the completion message. The new data is available after a successful load. An empty result can mean no match, a country filter, a minimum-character threshold, or missing master data. If enabled, ENFORCE VALID CALLSIGN separately checks the base call against the loaded country file before logging.

Source check

Earlier reference manual and wiki configuration statements for partial/possible calls and SCP. Current: trdos/logedit.pas (DoPossibleCalls, SuperCheckPartial), trdos/logscp.pas, uSettingsModel, and MainUnit candidate-key handlers. The current default keys are ,, ., and ;.

docs.title: Contest additions and rule checks
docs.text: Search the new-contest picker by part of the event's name. Read the event information and supply the operating area, category, and exchange requested for that contest. Existing logs can still open when an older event is hidden from the new-contest list.

docs.title: Contest additions through 5.1.0
docs.text:
5.1.0 adds RUS-WW-DIGI and the Weekly RTTY Test (WRT). See all 29 contests added since 4.x and the full 5.1.0 contest list. The combined IN7QPNE choice is for stations outside the participating areas.

Canadian Prairies is scheduled for the second Saturday in May at 17:00 UTC for 10 hours. The Atlantic Canada multiplier list uses 47 counties and divisions. Check the sponsor's schedule before the event.

  • Winter Field Day 2027 counts QSO points. Apply the objectives bonus at submission. TR4W excludes 12, 17, 30, and 60 m for this event.
  • ARRL Sweepstakes stores contacts in the wrong mode as rule-derived X-QSOs. FM does not qualify as Sweepstakes phone. In contests that exchange the year first licensed, such as EUHFC and KVP, enter MY LICENSE YEAR in the appropriate station or contest field.
  • QSO parties use contest-specific modes and scoring. Florida, Ohio and 7QP refuse FM. Indiana and Salmon Run accept CW and phone. Florida has contest-specific overlay and station categories. Check the sponsor's rules for mobile and rover bonuses and any manual claim.
  • Vermont QSO Party uses vtqp_club_stations.txt with a YEAR line for the yearly club multiplier list. Eligible digital contacts can produce a separate -ft.adi export.
  • RU3AX Memorial now uses a grid exchange. Older logs lacking grids can rescore to zero under the new rules.

docs.title: Operate as a rover
docs.text:
Type ROVER in the call field and press Enter, or choose Tools → Commands → ROVER. Select or enter your operating place or places and confirm. The dialog applies the contest's county-line limit. Watch the ROVER panel when moving, and use the same dialog to turn roving off.

At a boundary, one contact creates linked rows for the selected places. Dupe checking includes the place you sent from. Set your sent messages with {ROVERCALL} and {ROVERQTH} where appropriate. Review the export before submitting a rover log.

docs.title: Entering the exchange
docs.text:
Type the exchange as it is sent on the air, words separated by spaces. When TR4W knows a typed code is not valid for the contest, for example a district, state or section the contest does not list, or a CQ zone above 40, it refuses the entry and says why on the status line. Correct the word and press Enter again. Not every contest's parser names its reason yet; with the standard QSL mode, a refusal without a message still means the entry was not logged.

With QSL MODE set to QSL AND LOG, a refused entry is still logged. A refused zone is not written to the contact, but the exchange text is stored with the contact as typed, so the zone can be corrected afterwards.

RSGB IOTA references may be typed with or without the dash: EU-005, EU005 and EU-5 are all logged as EU-005. Only a dash straight after the continent is accepted.

docs.title: Check before submission
docs.text:
Confirm the exchange, multiplier totals, eligible bands and modes, and category. TR4W stores the contest's X-QSO decision separately from your manually set X-QSO flag. Edit QSO shows a rule-derived X-QSO as checked and disabled. Rescore Log recomputes the rule result using the current contest rules. Grid-based contests require the applicable grid information.

TR4W records station facts with each QSO, including applicable own-call, location, and zone information. Review these when operating from more than one location; changing today's station settings is not a substitute for correcting an earlier contact.

Export and inspect Cabrillo or ADIF, then follow the sponsor's submission instructions.

Review boundary

Based on RELEASE_NOTES.md, CHANGES.md, the contest registry and the individual 5.1.0 contest definitions. Check the sponsor's submission instructions for your event.

docs.title: Connect a DX cluster
docs.text:
The main-window status strip now shows the DX Cluster connection state even with the console closed. It identifies the subsystem; open the cluster window for the host and detailed messages.

The cluster console shows the node's messages and lets you send commands. Parsed DX spots feed the band map, where contest and display rules determine what you see.

docs.title: Connect and check reception
docs.text:
1. Choose Windows → DX Cluster.
  2. Use Configure... to review the cluster connection, then select the intended node.
  3. Choose Connect and follow any login prompts from that node.
  4. Confirm that node messages arrive. Use the command-entry field and Send for a command appropriate to the node.
  5. Compare a received spot with the band map. If the console receives it but the map does not show it, review the map filters and spot age.

The form also provides Disconnect, Freeze, Clear, Commands, and SH/50. Command support and response syntax depend on the cluster node; a button's presence does not make every server understand that command.

The host selector is at the left below the toolbar. Enter a node command in the field beside it. In the first spot from this local practice feed, K1ABC reported K3LR on 7012.3 kHz with the comment CW CQ PA. The timestamp at the right is UTC. The band map example uses the same feed.

Configure... opens Preferences → DX Cluster. Use Add... to enter a host and port, or choose a server from the supplied list.

Recognized SH/DX history replies can also populate the band map. Their age comes from the UTC time in the reply.

docs.title: Self-spot from the run frequency
docs.text:
Choose Control → Self-spot or put {SPOTME} in a function-key message. TR4W supplies your callsign, run frequency, and contest name. It checks the contest's self-spot rules, run state, frequency, and cluster connection before sending.

CLUSTER AUTO SELF SPOT is off by default. When enabled, CLUSTER SELF SPOT INTERVAL accepts 1–240 minutes and defaults to 10. A contest can require a longer minimum. Check the notice if a manual self-spot is refused.

docs.title: Freeze, clear, and history
docs.text:
Freeze lets you hold the console view for reading; it is not the Disconnect command. Clear concerns console content, not the contest's QSO database. Use the controls for their displayed purpose rather than using console visibility as a connection-status test.

The current code separates the visible console-line budget from the session trace. TELNET CONSOLE LINES bounds the displayed history; it is not a promise that the session archive is limited to the same number of lines.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom First check No connection Selected host/port, reachability, and the node's availability. Connected but no useful spots Login, node-side filters, and the node's supported commands. Console has spots but the map appears empty Band, mode, mult-only, dupe, and age filters. Old console lines are no longer visible Console-line budget; consult the session trace when diagnosing history.

A spot is information from another source. It can contain an incorrect call, stale frequency, or misleading comment. Verify it while operating.

Evidence and review status

UI: ui/lcl/uTelnetForm.lfm and .pas. Transport: uDXClusterClient.pas. Spot ingestion: uTelnet.pas, uDXSpotParse.pas, and uSpots.pas. Session logging: uTelnetTrace.pas. This page has not connected to a live cluster for validation.

docs.title: Keyboard essentials
docs.text: Learn a small set of commands in a practice contest before adding more. These bindings are taken from the current accelerator table, rather than the older shortcut inventory.

docs.title: Settings and log review
docs.text:
Keys Action Ctrl+J Open settings. Ctrl+L View / Edit log. Alt+L Search log. Ctrl+N Add a note. Ctrl+R Recall last entry. Alt+F Make a local log snapshot and, if configured, queue an external backup copy.

Check the backup result after Alt+F. An external destination is optional; check background-copy completion separately.

docs.title: Operating tools
docs.text:
Keys Action Alt+D Dupe check. Alt+P Open Fkeys. Alt+S CW speed. Alt+K In CW mode, turn CW sending off or on. In Phone, Digital and FM modes, turn the voice keyer (DVK) off or on instead. The menu item reads Toggle CW or Toggle Voice Keyer to match the current mode. Ctrl+U View packet spots. Ctrl+Y Refresh band map. Ctrl+T Repeat the saved POTA park exchange for another callsign. Ctrl+Enter Log QSO without CW.

Ctrl+Enter is a logging action: check the call and exchange before using it. Function-key messages depend on your configuration; review their contents before transmitting.

The function-key commands TOGGLECW and CWENABLETOGGLE behave the same way as Alt+K: they toggle CW in CW mode and the voice keyer in any other mode. The call-window commands CWON and CWOFF act on CW only, whatever the mode.

docs.title: Run a call-window command
docs.text:
Choose Tools → Commands, or type the complete command in the callsign field and press Enter. A recognized typed command clears the call field. Choosing the same action from the menu leaves any call you were entering in place.

Task Commands Export or report ADIF, CAB (Cabrillo), SUM (summary sheet) Log and operate NOTE, OPON (operator sign-in), ROVER, CWON, CWOFF Send over UDP SCORE (score), UDP (whole log) Query the DX cluster WCY (SH/WCY), WWV (SH/WWV) Open a tool or exit PREF, COL (colors), CMD (Windows command prompt), EXIT

The Rover example shows a dialog opened by a call-window command. Use the message command syntax when programming function keys.

docs.title: Focus and menu shortcuts
docs.text:
Menus now display assigned shortcuts in a separate column. In the main QSO-entry window, Ctrl+A opens keyboard CW; do not assume it selects all callsign text. Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, and Ctrl+A perform normal copy, paste, and select-all operations in focused text controls, including the cluster console and dialogs. Their effect depends on which window has focus.

Alt+- toggles autosend. PgUp, PgDn, Pause, and Ins can reach the operating actions from tool windows. The band map, log, and cluster console retain their own PgUp/PgDn paging behavior. Practice these actions with transmission disabled before relying on them during a contest.

docs.title: If a shortcut does not work
docs.text:
Return focus to the main operating window and check the matching menu item. A dialog, text field, desktop shortcut, or keyboard layout may affect delivery of the key combination. Record the operating system, active window, and exact combination when reporting a mismatch.

A focused reference

This is a selected list, not a complete keyboard specification. Context-sensitive entry keys and programmable messages require a separate operating walkthrough. The April inventory's “Ctrl+T is free” entry is superseded by the current POTA binding.

Source check

tr4w/src/uAccelerators.pas defines the displayed combinations and installed menu accelerators. Action labels and dispatch were checked in uMenu.pas, uTR4WStrings.pas, and MainUnit.pas. Actual delivery on each supported desktop has not been tested for this guide.

docs.title: Read the multiplier windows
docs.text: Multiplier windows answer “which multipliers have I worked, and which do I still need?” for the selected contest context. A multiplier is not the same as a new callsign: a new station can belong to a country, zone, or section you have already worked.

docs.title: Choose the relevant view
docs.text:
TR4W has a Remaining mults window and fixed views for DX, domestic, zone, and prefix multipliers. The general window follows the selected remaining-multiplier type; the fixed views keep their own type.

View What its entries represent DX Country/prefix identifiers from the country data. Domestic The contest's domestic multiplier list, such as sections or other defined areas. Zone Zone numbers for the active multiplier rules. Prefix Prefix multiplier entries.

Only the multiplier categories used by the contest are meaningful. A view's existence does not imply that category counts in every event.

docs.title: Understand worked and needed status
docs.text:
The display resolves each entry against current multiplier state when painting. Worked status is evaluated with band and mode context and the contest's multiplier rules; a multiplier worked elsewhere may still be needed on this band.

REMAINING MULT DISPLAY MODE controls which entries appear. In 5.1.0, an unworked multiplier is plain, a worked multiplier is black with white text, and a multiplier that still wants a backup is orange by default. A count appears from the second working. Use Preferences → Appearance → Colors to change BAND MAP WORKED MULT COLOR, the backup-needed color shared with the band map.

Open this view from Windows → Mults → Domestic. The Florida QSO Party practice log uses a target of two contacts per multiplier. Fl 2 has met the target, Ut has one contact and still needs a backup, and plain entries such as Ga are unworked.

SHOW DOMESTIC MULTIPLIER NAME uses the longer alternate domestic name when one is available, otherwise retaining the ordinary entry label.

Find both settings in Ctrl+J → Contest → Multiplier data.

docs.title: Check a surprising result
docs.text:
1. Confirm the contest, current band, and mode.
  2. Check the logged contact's call and exchange.
  3. Confirm that the contact represents the multiplier category being displayed.
  4. Compare the multiplier window with the log and score state after the display refreshes.

The window is a view of the program's multiplier calculation, not an independent validation of the contest rules. Test methodology explains how multiplier and export behavior are checked.

Evidence and review status

ui/lcl/uRemMultsForm.pas (MultTypeFor, MultsDrawCell), uRemMults.pas (cell resolution), uMults.pas, and uTestMults.pas. Layout, display modes, and examples in specific contests still need operator review.

docs.title: Operate POTA and park-to-park
docs.text: Select POTA when starting your contest. Use a practice log first to check park entry and exported fields.

docs.title: Set your own park
docs.text:
Open Ctrl+J → Station and enter your full park reference in Park under Contest exchange, for example US-0663. This identifies your park in the ADIF export and supplies the country prefix when you enter a digits-only worked-park reference. See the Station Preferences page.

Use Download POTA Parks in the Tools menu to update the park-name database before operating. The current code resolves the data location for the platform; the older wiki instruction that the download always lives beside the executable should not be assumed for this build.

docs.title: Enter a worked park
docs.text:
Enter the other station's callsign in the call field. In the exchange field, enter the signal report and the park reference, for example:

59 US-1274

Use the actual received report and park. The following examples illustrate the normalization rules:

What you type Interpretation US-1274 Full reference. US1274 Normalized to US-1274. 1274 Uses the country prefix from MY PARK; with US-0663, becomes US-1274. 59 A report, not a park reference.

Use a full reference when the worked park has a different country prefix from yours. If the local parks database contains the reference, check the displayed park name before logging.

docs.title: Work a station at multiple parks
docs.text:
Put each worked park in the same exchange, separated by spaces:

57 US-0663 US-1234

One Enter saves the park rows together. Check that the resulting entries have the same worked call, band, mode, and report, with a different park reference in each entry. The number of log entries can therefore exceed the number of on-air contacts.

These are example references, not a claim about which parks can be activated together.

docs.title: Repeat the exchange for another callsign
docs.text:
After logging the park exchange, use Ctrl+T or Repeat POTA Parks (2nd Op) to recall its park information. Check the exchange, enter the next worked callsign, and log the contact.

This command saves typing; it does not switch your own station identity or your own park. Explicitly check the callsign field before logging. If there is no saved POTA exchange in the session, the command reports that no parks have been logged yet.

docs.title: Check the ADIF before upload
docs.text:
Export ADIF, then inspect a single-park and a multi-park contact:

Field What to verify MY_SIG_INFO, MY_POTA_REF The activating park recorded with the QSO. SIG_INFO, POTA_REF The worked park when a recognized park reference is present. SRX_STRING The individual worked-park reference for each park entry.

Set MY PARK for the location before logging. ADIF uses the recorded park where available, and the current value for older rows that never recorded a station. Check representative entries from each activation before upload.

Evidence and review status

Adapted from the wiki's POTA-Operation.md. Current checks: uPOTAParks.pas; ProcessRSTAndPOTAPark in trdos/logstuff.pas; pending-park handling and HandleRepeatPOTAParks in MainUnit.pas; ADIF tail fields in trdos/postunit.pas; MY PARK binding in ui/lcl/uPrefsForm.pas. A field activation, multi-park sequence, and exported file still need an operator walkthrough.

docs.title: Radio 1 and Radio 2 windows
docs.text:
Choose Windows → Radio 1 or Windows → Radio 2. Each panel shows the VFOs and status of its own radio slot. The title can include the configured radio name.

This 20 m example shows a connected Elecraft K4. The Active label identifies the radio you are operating. Frequency readouts are in kHz, and enabled RIT, XIT, and SPLIT flags appear in yellow.

Field or indication Meaning VFO A and its mode Frequency and mode reported for the first VFO. VFO B and its mode Frequency and mode reported for the second VFO, where the driver supplies them. The inactive VFO frequency is greyed. RIT frequency Reported receive incremental tuning offset. RIT Yellow when receive incremental tuning is on. XIT Yellow when transmit incremental tuning is on. SPLIT Yellow when split operation is on. Check which VFO transmits at the radio. Status text Status supplied by the radio polling/interface layer. Active label and panel tint This radio has operating focus in TR4W. Spectrum button Opens this slot's panadapter when the connected radio both supports spectrum and currently makes it available.

These panels display what the driver reports; a model's registration does not guarantee every field is supported. Compare the panel with the front panel while commissioning a radio. For SO2R, keep both panels visible and verify the active radio before sending or logging. Each spectrum-capable slot has its own panadapter window.

For a frozen frequency or a disconnected interface, use the checks under Reset Radio Ports.

docs.title: Spectrum
docs.text:
Click Spectrum on the radio panel to view that radio's live spectrum and waterfall when the connected radio supplies spectrum data.

The spectrum trace plots signal level by frequency. The waterfall below shows recent activity, and the vertical A and B markers show the VFO frequencies.

docs.title: Main-window connection status
docs.text:
A strip at the bottom of the main window gives Radio 1, Radio 2, DX Cluster, and Network separate status panels. A condition stays until it changes or clears; an unrelated subsystem cannot overwrite it. Short notices, such as an imported-contact count, still appear on the message line and expire.

Cluster and network text identifies the subsystem. Open its own window for the host/address and full details. Radio panels show the current condition even when opened after a connection failure. A connected network socket alone is not enough to mark an Icom operational: authentication and its control stream must complete.

Saved main-window heights from older builds are adjusted for the new strip. Continue to resize vertically to control how many QSOs are visible.

Source check

ui/lcl/uRadioPanelForm.lfm and .pas, particularly LabelFor, SetFlag, SyncActiveTint, and OpenPanadapterForSlot; updates arrive through uPanelUpdate and uRadioPolling.

Select the exact event/mode when starting a contest. A selectable name means the program has a contest definition; it does not certify current sponsor rules, every exchange variation, or hardware/platform testing. Check the event rules and exercise an example exchange and export before operating.

docs.title: Available languages and translation status
docs.text: TR4W includes built-in English and 21 UI translation catalogues. A normal resource build embeds the translation catalogues. Check the language choices in your installed build.

docs.title: Test a language
docs.text:
Use the table’s --lang= argument when launching TR4W. Examples:

WindowsLinuxmacOS 
.\tr4w.exe --lang=it

./tr4w --lang=fr

open -a TR4W --args --lang=de

Close the running instance first so the argument is applied to a new launch. You can also save a choice in Preferences. Command-line language tags differ from three-letter translation-tool arguments such as ITA or FRA.

docs.title: How to interpret the counts
docs.text:
• Unflagged text: nonempty translation with no fuzzy flag. This includes inherited text and metadata; it is not a certificate of human review.
  • Needs review: nonempty text marked fuzzy. It may be a machine draft or a copied translation requiring context review.
  • Empty: no translation text, whether fuzzy or not. English fallback can remain visible.
  • Counts exclude the catalogue header and obsolete entries. Totals can differ between languages because their catalogues were refreshed at different times.

Earlier translation means the catalogue credits an earlier language contributor; new UI strings can still be machine-generated or missing. Italian and French have no inherited human translation baseline in this expansion: their LibreTranslate drafts require review, even where a few entries are not marked fuzzy. Treat the other newly seeded languages the same way.

English is compiled into the program as the source and fallback language.

docs.title: Review before calling a language complete
docs.text:
Review contest terminology and every machine draft, preserve formatting placeholders, then inspect real windows for clipping, keyboard markers, and meaning in context. The current test build includes fuzzy UI entries by default; language loading and ReviewedOnly behavior explain why unreviewed text can be visible.

Presence of a help catalogue does not establish its completeness. Its review workload is separate from the UI counts above.

docs.title: Provenance and regeneration
docs.text:
Counts: i18n/tr4w_*.po at source revision 4a0707be141d12c48327358c23deeddd2f0af0b7. Earlier contributor names come from the catalogues’ translation-author entries. New-language classification follows the project’s translation expansion and supplied editorial guidance; fuzzy flags alone cannot identify which tool wrote an individual phrase.

Run python tools/build_language_reference.py to refresh this table. This measures source catalogues, not the resources of an arbitrary downloaded binary.

docs.title: Earlier manuals and wiki
docs.text:
The TR4W wiki says it replaces the reference manual v4.01 and covers features through v4.147.07. It is valuable background for 5.x, but storage, dialogs, and platform support require another review.

Task Wiki source What to recheck for 5.x Find a command Configuration statements Setting names, defaults, persistence, and scope. Learn operating keys Windows and hot keys Current bindings, keyboard layout, OS behavior. Operate from parks POTA operation Dialog labels, multi-park entry, and exported ADIF. Set up digital logging WSJT-X integration Settings storage and current Reporting controls. Connect other software UDP broadcasts Message enablement, ports, and destination settings. Use two radios SO2R tips Hardware support and platform-specific keying.

The TR4W website links the older PDF user and reference manuals and labels them obsolete. They remain historical background, not the authority for a current 5.x procedure.

The local repository also contains docs/TR4W_Reference_Manual_4.01-1.md and docs/MANUAL_UPDATE_SUMMARY.md. The latter explains the earlier wiki update and is useful for planning the remaining migration.

docs.title: Radio support and connection reference
docs.text: 102 registrations extracted from the radio factory in this source snapshot. This is a declared driver/transport inventory, not a report of successful hardware tests.

docs.title: Read the table
docs.text:
• Native TR4W means a direct TR4W driver registration. It does not mean an operating-system release is production-ready.
  • Serial / Network are the transports explicitly registered for that driver. Network support does not imply discovery support.
  • Port and serial parameters are setup defaults, not requirements that override the radio’s actual configuration.
  • Hamlib only means the connection goes through a Hamlib backend. The registry exposes both transports generically; the backend and radio decide what works. A Hamlib model ID on a native radio is not proof it requires Hamlib.

docs.title: Important exceptions
docs.text:
• Expert TCI (HamLib bridge) is a retained placeholder. Its source says the shipped Hamlib backend is absent; do not treat that entry as a working alternative. The distinct native TCI (ExpertSDR / Thetis / AetherSDR) entry is documented in the TCI guide.
  • HamLib (any supported rig) uses a placeholder model ID; choose the actual rig’s Hamlib model ID during setup.
  • CW-by-CAT, spectrum, voice keying, and model-specific operating limits live in driver capability code. They are not inferred by this table.

docs.title: WSJT-X settings
docs.text:
The 5.1.0 settings model registers these names. Use the setup guide to connect the programs.

Setting Purpose WSJT-X ENABLED Enable the WSJT-X listener. WSJT-X BROADCAST PORT UDP port on which TR4W receives messages; must match the sending application. WSJT-X MULTICAST GROUP Multicast group to join; an empty value selects ordinary unicast. WSJT-X SEND HIGHLIGHTS Send callsign highlight information back to WSJT-X. WSJT-X RADIO CONTROL ENABLED Allow frequency changes from WSJT-X to move the radio.

The model documents an enabled listener and port 2237 as defaults. The port type restricts values to 1–65535.

The separate N1MM-style log listener uses ENABLE N1MM LOG LISTENER and N1MM LISTEN ADDRESS. Its default is off, with a loopback address of 127.0.0.1.

Names, not a file-editing recipe

This table documents supported command names. It does not imply that a particular settings file uses this text as its on-disk format. Use the settings UI for the current build.

Source: tr4w/src/uSettingsModel.pas, class TWsjtxSettings and the five Alias('WSJT-X ...') registrations. Source snapshot and review limits are recorded in Evidence and review.

docs.title: Read an entry
docs.text:
• Station settings belong to the station settings model; Contest settings are captured with the contest. Do not carry forward the old manual’s INI/CFG storage column as a current editing recipe.
  • Initial value means a direct literal in the source constructor. Loading a station, a contest definition, or a saved database can change it. An unextracted value is not an empty or zero default.
  • Values gives boolean choices or literal numeric type bounds when available. Other validation can apply; numeric bounds do not establish units.
  • Other accepted names are inventory aliases. They do not imply that every input route applies the value.
  • English settings help comes from the application catalogue. Follow the linked operator procedure where available.

Prefer the settings UI. Current command dispatch can recognize a name without applying it, depending on the caller and ownership. Recognition alone does not prove a legacy config line takes effect.

Normally, when you press a function key memory when a CW message is already playing, the previous message will be aborted and the new message started. docs.title: ALWAYS CALL BLIND CQ
docs.text:
Detail Current metadata Scope Station Values TRUE or FALSE Initial value in constructor False Other accepted names None listed

English settings help

This function is principally designed to be useful in contests like the Sprint when you are using TR4W with two rigs. In such a situation, you often want to send a CQ on the other rig while you are receiving the exchange from the station to whom you are about to cede the frequency. Normally you do this by pressing F7 or F8, which by default sends CQ on the inactive rig. Setting the ALWAYS CALL BLIND CQ function to TRUE causes that CQ to occur automatically as soon as the CQ EXCHANGE has been sent. (It sends whatever message is stored in Exchange memory F7.). Note that this does force you to be ready for that CQ by finding a clear frequency in time for it to be sent.

docs.text:
Detail Current metadata Scope Station Values TRUE or FALSE Initial value in constructor False Other accepted names None listed

English settings help

When using the bandmap or submitting packet spots in an environment in which you do not have a radio that communicates with TR4W, the program will normally ask you for the frequency of stations as you perform dupe checks. Setting this parameter to FALSE will stop TR4W from asking you for these frequencies.

docs.title: AUTO CALL TERMINATE
docs.text:
Detail Current metadata Scope Station Values TRUE or FALSE Initial value in constructor False Other accepted names None listed

English settings help

When you are on CW and this parameter is TRUE, TR4W can automatically terminate callsigns that you enter in response to a CQ. When coupled with the START SENDING NOW KEY or the AUTO SEND CHARACTER COUNT commands, TR-LOG will assume that a call is complete when all the characters entered in the Call Window have been transmitted. For example, assume that 4U1ITU has answered your CQ. If you press the key identified by the START SENDING NOW KEY command after entering 4U1I, the program will start to send 4U1I. If you enter one or more additional characters before it completes sending, TR-LOG will send those characters as well. If there are no new characters to send, it will automatically send the CQ EXCHANGE. TR4W works the same way if the AUTO SEND CHARACTER COUNT function causes the program to start sending the callsign. In this case, it is possible to respond to a station by using the same number of keystrokes that are in its callsign.

English settings help

The AUTO QSL INTERVAL command can be used to send the QUICK QSL MESSAGE instead, except that once every AUTO QSL INTERVAL QSOs, the QSL MESSAGE is transmitted instead. This is typically used when dealing with a large pileup. If you set AUTO QSL INTERVAL to 3, then the QUICK QSL MESSAGE would be sent, except for every third QSO. A value of zero disables this feature, in which case the QSL MESSAGE is sent at the end of every QSO.

docs.text:
Detail Current metadata Scope Station Values TRUE or FALSE Initial value in constructor False Other accepted names None listed

English settings help

If you press F2, you will send the next QSO number, which will be one more than the one you sent the first time. To fix this problem, you can set AUTO QSO NUMBER DECREMENT to TRUE; this causes TR4W to decrement the QSO number when you press F2 when both the Call Window and the Exchange Window are empty.

docs.title: AUTO SEND CHARACTER COUNT
docs.text:
Detail Current metadata Scope Station Values 0–6 (numeric type bounds; see description for units) Initial value in constructor 0 Other accepted names None listed

English settings help

TR4W can start to send the callsign of a station responding to your CQ after you have typed a certain number of characters in the callsign of the calling station. This number of characters is controlled with the AUTO SEND CHARACTER COUNT command. For example, if you set AUTO SEND CHARACTER COUNT to 3 and 4U1ITU calls you, the program will start sending the call after you have typed 4U1. If you enable the AUTO CALL TERMINATE feature, the program will transmit the CQ EXCHANGE message when it has sent all the characters you have typed. When the AUTO SEND CHARACTER COUNT is non-zero, an arrow will appear above the Call Window to indicate the point at which TR4W will begin to transmit the callsign. You can disable this function with the Alt-- command. The arrow will then disappear. To re-enable it, press Alt-- again and the arrow will reappear. You can delete any unsent characters with the backspace key.

docs.title: CLUSTER SPOT COMMENT MULTIPLIER
docs.text:
Detail Current metadata Scope Station Values TRUE or FALSE Initial value in constructor False Other accepted names None listed

English settings help

When this parameter is set to TRUE and the contest looks its domestic multiplier (section or state) up in its domestic file, a DX cluster spot whose comment names a section or state is shown as a needed multiplier when that one is needed. The first UPPER CASE word of the comment that the contest's domestic file knows is used; a section the cluster appends with a plus sign (+NC) is used only when no earlier word qualifies. A section already known for the station from the call history or from a contact in the log overrules the comment. Beacon spots (NCDXF) are ignored. Not every spot has one, and the cluster's section can be where a station lives rather than where it is operating, so leave this FALSE unless you want it.

1. Current settings inventory, checked against the frozen command vocabulary, supplies names, aliases, scopes, and types.
  2. Current model declarations verify every inventory property/type and supply literal initial values and numeric subranges.
  3. Current uCFG dispatch lists distinguish withdrawn names, store-owned names, and actions.
  4. Reviewed descriptions override the English settings help in i18n/help_en.po. Historical INI defaults appear separately.
  5. The old manual supplies historical names and the migration lookup; its extracted PDF layout is too inconsistent to safely promote whole definition blocks automatically.

The older CTRLJ_INVENTORY, CFG_COMMAND_TABLE, and HELP_TEXT_GAPS documents explain the migration but contain historical counts and architecture. They are not the current command list.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
These commands do work rather than simply storing a preference. They are handled separately in TryApplyCommandAction; do not document them as persistent checkboxes.

Command Current handler behavior ADD DOMESTIC COUNTRY Adds a country to the domestic list; CLEAR clears that list. CLEAR DUPE SHEET Records the requesting config file as the clear-dupe instruction; its value is ignored. BAND MAP CUTOFF FREQUENCY Parses an integer and adds a band-map mode cutoff. FREQUENCY MEMORY Adds a band/mode frequency memory; the handler distinguishes SSB-prefixed values.

docs.title: MAIN CALLSIGN
docs.text:
Detail Current metadata Scope Station Values Text Initial value in constructor '' Other accepted names None listed

English settings help

Your station's own callsign, remembered from contest to contest. The New Contest dialog fills its callsign box from it (or from MY CALL when this is empty), and the first callsign you enter there is saved here if it is empty. It is not the callsign you log with: that is MY CALL, which a contest may change (for example to a club call) without touching this one.

Detail Current metadata Scope Station Values Text Initial value in constructor '' Other accepted names None listed

English settings help

Values: Integer Normally, your zone is determined by your callsign. However, if you want TR4W to place you in a different zone, use this command. It is best to put this command before the CONTEST statement in your *.CFG file, so that TR4W will configure the contest properly. However, the relationship between what happens when the contest executes the MY ZONE command and when it executes the CONTEST command is complex, and under some circumstances (for example, the IARU contest) the MY ZONE command should appear after the CONTEST command. The most common symptom of having these commands in the incorrect order is that TR4W will score the contest as if you were in a different zone from the one in which you are actually located. If you see that TR4W does not seem to be scoring the contest properly, you should try switching

docs.title: NETWORK HTTP TRANSPORT
docs.text:
Detail Current metadata Scope Station Values Text Initial value in constructor 'generic' Other accepted names None listed

English settings help

Chooses what carries TR4W's internet requests: the downloads (country file, TRMASTER, call history, POTA parks, version check) and the uploads (the external logging services, HamScore, contest scores, SuperCheckPartial). generic is TR4W's own connection code, which checks server certificates against the cacert.pem shipped with the program. auto and platform use the operating system's own connection code where this platform has one (Windows only, today: WinHTTP). It trusts the Windows certificate store, follows the system proxy settings and needs no cacert.pem. Where there is none, both use generic, and platform says so in the log. A change applies from the next request, with no restart. A request that fails is never repeated on the other transport. The Windows transport is new: leave this on generic unless you were asked to try it.

Evidence and historical context

docs.title: QSL MODE
docs.text:
Detail Current metadata Scope Contest Values Text Initial value in constructor 'NONE' Other accepted names None listed

English settings help

Values: STANDARD, QSL AND LOG, or QSL BUT NO LOG. This command can be used to change the criteria used to QSL an exchange and to log it when you are in CQ Mode. Normally, TR4W requires the complete exchange to be entered before you can QSL and log the contact. However, if you select QSL BUT NO LOG, the QSL message will be sent even if the exchange information is not completed, but you need to finish entering the exchange and hit <Enter> again before it will be logged. QSL AND LOG will totally eliminate any syntax checking on the exchange and log whatever you have entered. This mode is NOT recommended in normal operations.
