docs.title: SERVER USE TAILCAT
docs.text:
Detail Current metadata Scope Station Values TRUE or FALSE Initial value in constructor False Other accepted names None listed

English settings help

Set to TRUE to reach TR4WSERVER through the Tailcat tunnel named by SERVER TAILCAT ADDRESS instead of at SERVER ADDRESS. While it is TRUE, SERVER ADDRESS is not used; SERVER PORT still is, because it is the server's port inside the tunnel. If SERVER TAILCAT ADDRESS is empty the connection fails and says so; TR4W does not fall back to SERVER ADDRESS. Set it to FALSE when you are on the server's own network; the address is kept for next time.

Evidence and historical context

Model path: Settings.Server.UseTailcat. Source type: boolean.

docs.title: Update country, callsign, and park data
docs.text:
Update reference data before an event, then verify the affected lookup in a practice contest. A successful download and a successful reload are separate steps.

Dataset Used for Update action CTY.DAT Country/prefix lookup used by contest calculations Country-file download action; Alt+O in the current accelerator table. TRMASTER.DTA Super Check Partial/callsign assistance Download TRMASTER.DTA. Contest call history Known exchange information such as a Sweepstakes check and section Help → Download call history for this contest, where available. pota_parks.csv Park-reference lookup and displayed park names Download POTA Parks. .DOM files Contest-specific domestic multiplier definitions Obtain the correct contest definition/data set; these are not the CTY or TRMASTER download.

docs.title: Download and check
docs.text:
1. Finish any active operating task and retain a backup of the contest before changing data used for scoring.
  2. Select the appropriate download action and wait for its completion or error report.
  3. Check the destination if diagnosing a failure. Downloads use the settings directory, or the directory of the explicit --settings file, rather than the application bundle.
  4. In 5.1.0 a successful TRMASTER or call-history load takes effect in the running application. If the new file fails validation or loading, TR4W continues using the previous data. Follow the program's message for other data files.
  5. Check a known call/prefix or park reference. For POTA, confirm that the expected park name appears.

CTY, TRMASTER, and park data solve different problems. Updating the callsign database does not update country boundaries or domestic multiplier definitions. A callsign suggestion is assistance, not evidence that it is the station you heard.

docs.title: If an update fails
docs.text: Read the diagnostic message for network, TLS, or destination-write errors. Confirm that the active settings directory is writable and that the download was for the intended station profile. Do not overwrite files inside a read-only AppImage or signed application bundle to work around a failed download.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text: Current actions and destinations: MainUnit.pas, uMenu.pas, uAppPaths.pas. Downloaders: uCTYUpdate.pas, uTRMasterUpdate.pas, and uPOTAParks.pas. The TRMASTER downloader names https://tr4w.net/TRMASTER.DTA; the POTA module names https://pota.app/all_parks_ext.csv. Endpoint availability was not tested for this documentation update.

docs.title: Files and folders
docs.text: The contest log contains your contacts. The diagnostic log, tr4w.log, records program activity and errors. They are different files with different purposes.

docs.title: Default locations
docs.text:
~ means your home directory. On Windows, “working folder” means the process's current directory, normally established by its shortcut or launch command; it is not always the executable's folder.

File group Windows under Program Files Windows in a writable folder macOS Linux Station settings %APPDATA%\TR4W\settings\tr4w.json working folder/settings/tr4w.json ~/Library/Application Support/TR4W/tr4w.json ~/.config/tr4w/tr4w.json Diagnostic log %APPDATA%\TR4W\tr4w.log working folder/tr4w.log ~/Library/Logs/TR4W/tr4w.log ~/.local/state/tr4w/tr4w.log Default contest root %APPDATA%\TR4W\ Working folder ~/tr4w/ ~/tr4w/ Shipped reference data Working folder Working folder TR4W.app/Contents/Resources/ /usr/share/tr4w/, with fallback beside the binary Downloaded CTY/TRMASTER/POTA data Settings directory Settings directory Settings directory Settings directory

TR4W 5.1.0 also uses the per-user location when a Windows working folder elsewhere refuses writes. It reports the redirect at startup. If you launch from a custom shortcut, check its Start in folder and the reported paths.

On Linux, XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME override the .config and .local/state bases. A --settings <path> launch option selects a different settings file and also relocates downloaded data beside that file. Opening a contest elsewhere does not imply that the station settings moved with it.

Local log snapshots are stored in a backup subfolder of the writable settings directory. BACKUP DESTINATION adds an optional background copy. See Back up your log. Passwords and API keys in the OS credential store are separate from the settings file.

docs.title: Example directory trees
docs.text:
These examples use practice.db as an illustrative contest filename. You can open a contest elsewhere; these show the default roots. Downloaded files appear after you obtain them, and SQLite companion files need not always be present.

WindowsmacOSLinux

Example working folder: C:\TR4W.

C:\TR4W\
├── settings\

│   ├── CTY.DAT          downloaded country data
│   ├── TRMASTER.DTA     downloaded callsign data

Use Preferences → Logging → Open log file to locate the active diagnostic log instead of guessing which installation produced it. See Diagnostic logging for DEBUG/TRACE settings and subsystem traces.

docs.title: File types
docs.text: File Purpose Contest .db SQLite contest database: contacts and contest-associated data. .db-wal, .db-shm SQLite companion files that can exist while a database is in use. Do not discard them while copying or recovering a live database. tr4w.json Station configuration. Use Preferences or the migration tool rather than assuming an older INI edit applies. Legacy .CFG / .TRW Earlier configuration and binary log formats; preserve originals during migration. .ADI ADIF export for transferring contacts. Cabrillo .LOG Contest submission output; distinct from the diagnostic tr4w.log. .DOM Domestic-multiplier definitions used by the contest. Shipped sets live in the data root's dom directory. CTY.DAT Country/prefix information. TRMASTER.DTA Callsign/Super Check Partial reference data. pota_parks.csv POTA park-reference and name lookup.

docs.title: DOM files and contest-specific data
docs.text:
The DOMESTIC FILENAME setting identifies the domestic multiplier file. Contest definitions can select their own data, and DOM files can include other definitions from the shipped DOM directory. Preserve custom DOM files with the contest archive and record which version you used.

Do not move a working setup's custom data merely to match a generic table. The configured filename and the program's diagnostic messages are the authority for a particular contest.

docs.title: Download precedence
docs.text:
For data using the preferred-data resolver, the downloaded copy beside the active settings file wins over the shipped copy. This lets the application update data without modifying a signed macOS bundle or a read-only Linux package. A newer application package can still use an older downloaded override until you update that override.

For a live contest backup, use TR4W's snapshot procedure. For an archive, close the application and preserve the contest files, relevant settings, and custom reference data.

Source check

Paths and precedence: uAppPaths.pas (tr4w/src/uAppPaths.pas). DOM handling: trdos/logdom.pas. Export names: trdos/postunit.pas and the corpus README. The Linux installation document's older “beside the binary” contest location is superseded by ContestDir.

docs.title: Open your first contest
docs.text: Use a practice log to become familiar with TR4W before entering a live contest.

docs.title: Complete the initial station setup
docs.text:
On the first launch, choose Yes when TR4W offers the Setup Wizard. On Your station, enter your callsign and check the station details.

When the initial setup prompts for your grid square, enter the Maidenhead locator for the station's operating location. For example, FN31 is a four-character locator and FN31PR is a six-character locator; use your own location, not these examples. Follow the length requested by the prompt or contest.

Check both your callsign and grid before continuing. You can review or change Grid square later in Ctrl+J → Station. If you operate portable or move the station, check it again for the new location. TR4W uses the station grid for headings, distances, and applicable exported station information. See the Station Preferences page.

Choose Next to select any equipment or services you want to configure now. Leave the boxes clear and choose Create configuration to finish with station details only.

To revisit setup later, choose Tools → Setup Wizard, or launch TR4W with --wizard.

docs.title: Create a contest
docs.text:
1. Start TR4W. In Open configuration file or start a new contest, find Start a new contest.
  2. Enter your station callsign in Callsign.
  3. Search for part of the event name and select it in CONTEST. Turn on Upcoming contests first to sort by the next known occurrence. Read the event information and complete the requested operating area, county, category, and sent exchange as applicable.
  4. Choose OK.
  5. Check the contest and station information before entering contacts. See what each main window field shows and configure your radio if you want frequency and mode information from the rig.

TR4W opens the dupe sheet for a NON-ASSISTED entry and the band map for an ASSISTED entry, using the contest's CATEGORY-ASSISTED value.

docs.title: Reopen a contest
docs.text:
Under Open an existing configuration, select a log or use Browse.... The recent-log grid shows contest, year, call, last QSO, contact count, and file, with recent activity first. Last Contest reopens the most recent contest.

While operating, File → Open Log opens the same picker. Selecting a different contest restarts TR4W to load that contest.

The current picker lists contest .db files. It also lists a legacy .CFG when no corresponding .db exists. Opening a legacy contest can start migration; use a copy when evaluating the preview. See Moving from 4.x.

docs.title: Check the whole workflow
docs.text:
Before using your station for an event, verify these outcomes in a practice log:

Check Expected outcome Contest selection The exchange fields match the event you selected. Station location MY GRID matches the location from which you will operate. Radio tuning The displayed frequency follows the connected rig. Contact entry A completed practice contact appears in the log with the expected call, exchange, band, and mode. Reopening The practice contact is present after closing and reopening the contest. Export The exported log contains the contact and the expected station information.

Keep practice contacts separate from the log you will submit.

Continue with keyboard essentials, backups, and ADIF/Cabrillo export.

Source check

Labels and selection behavior: tr4w/src/ui/lcl/uNewContestForm.lfm and uNewContestForm.pas. The checklist is an editorial acceptance exercise, not a report of a completed UI test.

docs.title: Convert INI settings to JSON
docs.text: tr4wconvert brings legacy station settings into the current JSON settings file. It is a separate utility for users bringing existing settings from an older Windows installation; it does not convert your contest log or complete every part of contest migration. New Linux and macOS installations start with fresh settings and do not require this conversion.

docs.title: Recommended sequence
docs.text:
1. Close TR4W and preserve the old installation, tr4w.ini, and any existing tr4w.json.
  2. Install the intended 5.x package, including its matching tr4wconvert utility.
  3. Place a copy of the legacy tr4w.ini beside the destination settings file. If JSON does not exist yet, use the directory where it will be created.
  4. Run tr4wconvert from a terminal. Review the printed settings path, INI path, proposed changes, skipped contest settings, and refused values.
  5. Apply only when the report describes the intended source and destination. The interactive answer defaults to No.
  6. Start TR4W and verify callsign, radio/keyer setup, integrations, and other station preferences. Keep the original files until that check is complete.

The preferred sequence is install → convert → start TR4W. The converter can create a missing JSON file from defaults plus the legacy settings. It can also operate on an existing JSON file, so review the report carefully if the new program has already been used.

docs.title: Preview without writing
docs.text:
Run the matching executable from its installed location. On Windows, for an explicitly selected destination:

.\tr4wconvert.exe --settings "C:\TR4W\settings\tr4w.json" --report-only

That example reads C:\TR4W\settings\tr4w.ini by default. Substitute your actual location. Do not look for this utility as a required Linux or macOS installation step.

With no explicit settings path, the utility first considers a settings folder beside itself, then the platform settings location. Always read the reported path; the shell's current directory is not a reliable substitute for that check.

The first-run migration launcher now passes the detected legacy INI path explicitly, including when the destination JSON is in a custom settings directory. Review both paths before accepting conversion.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Behavior No mode option Report, then ask to apply if standard input is a terminal. --report-only Report without prompting or writing. --apply Write without prompting; intended for deliberate scripted use. --settings <path> Select the destination settings file. --no-ini Do not read an INI file. --all Include every command in the report. --ini <path> Still accepted, but deprecated; names a nondefault legacy INI.

When run without an interactive terminal and without --apply, the utility reports and writes nothing. Exit code 0 includes an operator declining conversion; it is not proof that a file was written. 1 indicates a settings-read failure; 2 indicates one or more refused values. Review the report as well as the exit code.

docs.title: Scope and limits
docs.text:
Contest-scoped settings belong in the contest database and are reported/skipped by this tool. Contact data and contest messages need their own migration checks. See Import contacts and Moving from 4.x.

Conversion of an older JSON commands bucket is a different path: the converter's current program header says TR4W startup now imports and collapses those legacy setting locations itself. Do not confuse that JSON cleanup with importing a 4.x INI file.

Source check

tr4wconvert.lpr (tr4w/tools/tr4wconvert/tr4wconvert.lpr) is the authority for arguments, discovery, prompting, and exit codes. uSettingsConvert.pas implements conversion, but some of its introductory startup comments predate later changes. No personal settings were converted while preparing this page.

docs.title: Install TR4W
docs.text:
Choose the package for your operating system and CPU from the TR4W-D12 releases. This guide covers 5.1.0. Check the asset name and read the notes supplied with your chosen release.

TR4W runs natively on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Start at the TR4W website or the project's release channel and select the intended version; these pages document 5.x.

WindowsLinuxmacOS
  1. Obtain tr4w_setup_<version>-x64.exe or the corresponding complete preview package from the project's release channel. Current 5.x Windows builds require 64-bit Windows. Use 4.x on a 32-bit Windows system.
  2. Close TR4W before replacing an existing installation. Preserve your contest files and settings.
  3. Run the installer, or extract the complete preview package into a writable location according to its supplied instructions. Keep required libraries and data with the application.
  4. When moving from 4.x, run the INI-to-JSON converter before the first normal launch.
  5. Launch using the installed shortcut. A Program Files installation keeps writable files under %APPDATA%\TR4W. The Start menu's Release notes shortcut opens the notes included with the installer.

Native preview packages include a tarball and an AppImage. Choose the package compatible with your system using the requirements below.

TR4W runs natively on macOS. The 5.0.26 release provides signed and Apple-notarized downloads for Apple Silicon (aarch64-darwin). These are not Intel Mac packages.

Download How to install Includes multi-op server? .pkg — installer Double-click the package and follow Installer. It installs TR4W.app in /Applications. No .dmg — disk image Open the image and drag TR4W.app to Applications, then eject the image. Yes, tr4wserver is beside the app in the image. .tar.gz — archive Extract the archive, keep the app bundle intact, and copy it to Applications. Yes, beside the app in the extracted payload.

For a normal desktop installation, download the Apple Silicon .pkg for the version you intend to run. Close any running TR4W instance before installing an update, complete Installer, then open Applications → TR4W and confirm the version. Station setup, including callsign and grid, happens in TR4W after installation.

All three formats carry the same application build. Choose the disk image or archive if this Mac must also run the multi-op server; the installer alone does not install it. Installing the app does not start a server automatically.

The .dSYM.zip archives and symbols-…txt manifest are diagnostic aids for alpha/beta testing, not installers or runtime dependencies. You do not need them to run TR4W. See crash reporting.

The published packages have stapled notarization tickets. Normal installation does not require removing quarantine attributes or disabling Gatekeeper.

Keep contest files and downloaded updates outside the bundle. The application writes operator files under your home directory. If macOS rejects a package, retain the exact message and request a correctly packaged build; this guide does not require disabling system protections.

docs.title: Linux requirements and troubleshooting
docs.text:
These requirements describe the preview packages reviewed for this guide. Check the requirements supplied with a newer package rather than assuming its build dependencies are identical.

Component Tarball Reviewed AppImage glibc 2.34 or newer 2.38 or newer, because bundled libraries require newer symbols GTK2 Install the distribution's GTK2 runtime Bundled SQLite Requires libsqlite3.so.0 Bundled OpenSSL Needed for TLS connections, online updates, and score posting Bundled Hamlib Install libhamlib.so.4 if using a Hamlib-backed radio Not bundled; host-library use needs testing with the package

Run ldd --version in a terminal to check glibc. An error such as GLIBC_2.34 not found means the tarball needs a newer runtime than the system provides. An AppImage does not eliminate the glibc requirement. Do not replace the operating system's C library manually to launch TR4W; use a compatible package or OS.

For the tarball, install runtime libraries through your distribution's package manager. Debian-family package names include libgtk2.0-0 or libgtk2.0-0t64, libsqlite3-0, and the OpenSSL runtime matching the release. Fedora uses gtk2, sqlite-libs, and openssl-libs; Arch uses gtk2, sqlite, and openssl. Package availability and exact names depend on the distribution release. The sqlite3 command-line tool alone is not a substitute for the SQLite shared library, and TR4W does not require the SQLite development package.

For an AppImage, make the actual downloaded file executable with chmod +x and launch it. If FUSE mounting fails, add --appimage-extract-and-run to that launch command. Keep the full tarball contents together when using the tarball, then run ./tr4w from the extracted directory.

A missing-Hamlib message matters only if you selected a Hamlib-backed radio; native TR4W radio drivers do not require it. Check the radio support table before installing an optional backend. Windows DLL plug-ins cannot be assumed to work on Linux, and CPU-generated CW has platform limitations.

Both package formats use the same operator file locations: contest databases default to ~/tr4w, with settings and diagnostic logs in their separate user directories. Nothing should be stored inside an AppImage. For startup problems, record the distribution/version, package filename, exact error, glibc version, and the diagnostic log if one was created.

docs.title: First-launch checks
docs.text:
Confirm the version, language, callsign, and writable file locations. Enter your station's Maidenhead grid locator when prompted during initial setup; see initial station setup. Create a practice contest, save and reopen a contact, and test backups. Then check the radio, keying method, and integrations individually.

Keep the previous working installation and its files until the new setup has passed your station's checks. Platform support remains a release-specific statement, especially for CW timing and external hardware.

docs.title: Build-source references
docs.text:
Windows/build documentation (tr4w/docs/BUILD.md) · macOS build wrapper and caveats (tr4w/build/build-mac.sh) · Unix packaging implementation (tr4w/build/build-unix.sh)

These installation paths have not been exercised on all three platforms for this documentation update.

docs.title: Moving from 4.x
docs.text:
The 5.x contest picker works with database logs. Some instructions in the older manual refer to files and storage that have since changed.

Treat station and contest migration as separate tasks: convert station INI settings to JSON, then import and verify contact data. Neither step alone confirms that your messages and contest-specific configuration are correct.

docs.title: Upgrade an existing 5.x database
docs.text: TR4W 5.1.0 opens contest logs at schema 13. On first open it verifies a backup of an older database before upgrading it. An earlier TR4W build that supports only an earlier schema will refuse the upgraded database. Keep the pre-upgrade snapshot and use a copy of that snapshot if you need to reopen the contest in the earlier build. Multi-op stations also need to upgrade the server and clients together.

docs.title: Try an older contest on a copy
docs.text:
1. Close the old TR4W instance and copy the entire contest folder to a separate test location.
  2. Start the 5.x preview and use Browse... in the opening dialog to select the copied legacy configuration.
  3. Allow the program to open the contest, then check the calls, exchanges, number of contacts, and contest selection.
  4. Close and reopen the migrated contest and check it again.
  5. Keep the original folder until you have compared an export from the migrated log with your original records.

The picker lists a legacy .CFG only when its matching .db is absent. Its implementation explains that opening a legacy contest builds the database from the binary log on first open; once the database exists, the picker avoids listing both entries.

Migration is not a backup

Work on the copied folder during this evaluation. This prototype has not tested round-trip compatibility or recovery of a live contest database. For subsequent backups of an open 5.x log, use the verified backup procedure.

docs.title: Settings also changed
docs.text:
Do not assume that an old instruction to edit tr4w.ini describes the current settings store. The current code has a typed settings model and the Linux notes identify ~/.config/tr4w/tr4w.json as the settings file. Prefer the program's settings controls while evaluating the preview.

Source check

tr4w/src/ui/lcl/uNewContestForm.pas (PopulateFiles), tr4w/src/uSettingsModel.pas, and docs/INSTALL_LINUX.md. Full migration, backup, and recovery procedures remain review tasks.

docs.title: Find and save settings
docs.text:
Open Preferences with Ctrl+J. Use the search box to find a setting by name, or choose a task in the tree.

The old More settings placeholder has been removed. Settings now belong to their relevant task pages. Search is the quickest route when a setting has moved.

docs.title: Save changes
docs.text:
Save writes changes and keeps Preferences open. Save and close writes them and closes the window. Cancel discards pending changes. Check each setting's help and restart notice: some changes apply immediately; others need a restart.

For external loggers, saving applies enable/disable and ordering immediately. New logger definitions and changed connections need a restart. For radios, FREQUENCY POLL RATE is now in that radio's Advanced settings, so configure each radio separately.

Passwords and API keys use the operating system's credential store. A settings-file backup alone does not move these secrets to another machine.

docs.title: Contest pages and station defaults
docs.text:
Contest settings include QSO settings, Modes, Initial exchange, Multiplier data, Quick QSL, QTC, Contest rules, and Cabrillo headings. The initial-exchange and call-history filename controls have browse buttons.

The Station page shows the open contest's values when it defines its own. When you change such a value, choose Station default only or Also this contest. Review any separate offer to correct older QSOs. Individual contacts retain the station facts sent when they were logged.

Hover over a control for help or search the command reference by its configuration name.

docs.title: Choose your version
docs.text:
Check the version shown by your TR4W build before choosing instructions.

What you are running Start here Public Windows 4.x release Use the TR4W website for downloads and the wiki for its manual. TR4W 5.1.0 Follow this guide. See log upgrades and multi-op compatibility before upgrading. FreePascal/Lazarus 5.x preview Use this guide as a draft companion to your build's release notes. Native Linux 5.x preview Read Linux requirements and troubleshooting in this guide. Native macOS 5.x TR4W runs natively on macOS. See the installation guide for .pkg, .dmg, and archive installation choices.

docs.title: Native desktop builds
docs.text:
This version runs natively on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Use the package built for your platform and CPU. Platform-specific hardware and packaging notes still apply.

The Linux packages covered here are preview builds. The tarball and AppImage have different glibc requirements. See installation requirements and CW sending options for platform limitations. Package requirements depend on how the artifact was built.

docs.title: What this guide verifies
docs.text:
The November 22, 2026 refresh covers the 5.1.0 tag at 4a0707be1. The command, contest, radio, and language tables use that source. Older screenshots retain their original version labels. See recent guide updates for the review scope and evidence for remaining operator checks.

Evidence and outstanding reviews

docs.title: Program CW function keys
docs.text:
TR4W retains the manual's separate message banks for running and search-and-pounce operation. The same function key can send a different message in each operating context.

  1. Select CW and open Settings → Program messages.
  2. Choose C for a CQ function key, E for an exchange/search-and-pounce function key, or O for other messages.
  3. Select the message to edit. Enter the transmitted content in Message and a useful button description in Caption.
  4. Open List of commands, select a command, and choose OK to insert it.
  5. Choose OK to apply the message. Test the key in the intended CQ or exchange context with the correct radio and CW sending backend. Function-key memories are captured in the contest database when the log closes; exit normally and reopen the practice log to check persistence. Do not edit the .db as though it were an old .cfg text file.

Alt+P opens the current message list. The screenshots show CW Open practice messages in TR4W 5.1.0 for Windows. CW Open exchanges a serial and name. In CWT, call CQ CWT and exchange your first name plus your CWops member number or, for non-members, your state, province, or DX country prefix.

docs.title: Start with simple messages
docs.text:
Message text Meaning CQ TEST \ \ CQ followed by your configured callsign twice. @ 5NN # The entered callsign, a CW signal report, and the serial number selected by TR4W's serial-number logic. Use only for a contest whose exchange fits. TU \ Thanks followed by your own callsign.

\ expands your configured callsign; @ expands the call being worked; # uses the serial-number logic, including configured leading zeros and abbreviated digits. These are executable message characters, so punctuation is not necessarily transmitted literally. A fixed-zone or section contest needs its actual exchange instead of the serial-number example.

Test each bank separately, including the exchange sent by the normal Enter workflow. Esc stops CW/automatic-CQ activity through the active sending path. Check the selected radio before testing a message that changes radio focus.

docs.title: Message commands
docs.text:
Use braces around a command. The editor upgrades recognized commands saved with the old control-character bookends. A leading $ inside the braces directs a radio command to the inactive radio.

In a contest that sends a signal report and location, insert {ROVERQTH} after the report.

Message text Effect {SPEED+} Increase CW speed. {ALT-D} Dupe check on radio 2. {SPAN=+} / {$SPAN=+} Widen the panadapter on the active or inactive radio, respectively. {ROVERCALL} / {ROVERQTH} Send the roving callsign or place. {SPOTME} Request a self-spot. PLS QSY {PASS B} Send a CW message with network station B's current frequency in kHz. A station name or band such as {PASS 14000} can also select a peer. {LASTPASSEDFREQ} Send the last frequency resolved by {PASS …}, for example 14025R5 for 14,025.5 kHz.

If a required pass frequency cannot be resolved, TR4W displays the reason and skips sending the message. Check the radio and the SO2R workflow before testing a command that changes radio focus.

Source check

Earlier wiki SO2R tips and reference manual message concepts. Current chooser/editor: uProgramMessageForm, uEditMessageForm (SaveToConfig), and uMessagesListForm; expansions: trdos/logsend.pas; stopping: MainUnit.Escape_proc. These examples have been checked against code, not transmitted on a radio.

docs.title: Choose a CW sending method
docs.text:
TR4W's CW sending layer selects one active method for sending text. Radio CAT control, CW generation, PTT, and two-radio output routing are related but separate parts of station setup.

Method What generates the CW What to check CW by CAT The radio receives text through its supported control protocol and keys it Model capability, connection, speed, buffering, and stop behavior. WinKeyer An external WinKeyer device Correct keyer port, successful device connection, output routing, and speed control. YCCC SO2R+ The external YCCC device Device connection, selected output, and SO2R configuration. CPU/software keyer TR4W supplies timed keying through the configured output Output line configuration and platform timing support.

The radio reference identifies transport support, not a complete CW capability matrix. A network connection or native driver alone does not establish CW-by-CAT support.

docs.title: Selection precedence
docs.text:
The current selector chooses CW by CAT when active, otherwise an active WinKeyer, otherwise an active YCCC device, and finally the CPU keyer. Configuration and successful activation are not interchangeable: a WinKeyer that never opens is not the active device.

Avoid configuring several methods and assuming they send together. The code reports conflicts because CW-by-CAT can take precedence over a hardware keyer for the active radio.

docs.title: Configure and test
docs.text:
1. Select the intended method for your radio and platform.
  2. For an external keyer, open Ctrl+J → Hardware → CW keyers and add or edit the device. For a WinKeyer, choose WINKEYER for Keyer type and select the connected device's Port.
  3. For software keying, review the radio's separate keyer-output and RTS/DTR controls. CAT port settings alone do not configure those lines.
  4. Review the function-key text with Alt+P before sending it. Use Alt+S to review CW speed.
  5. With an appropriate station test setup, check a short message, a longer buffered message, speed changes, and cancellation with Esc.
  6. In a two-radio station, verify which output keys and that switching radios does not leave an earlier message transmitting.

The CAT path has a specific sole-transmitter interlock because two radios have independent CW buffers. Hardware keyers route a shared keying engine to an output; their switching behavior is different. Test both routing and message cancellation with the actual station hardware.

docs.title: Platform limits
docs.text: The Linux preview notes identify gaps in host-timed CW. Do not assume CPU keying has the same timing behavior on every platform, or that an older manual's LPT instructions apply. External-device and CAT paths have their own verification requirements.

docs.title: Related settings and evidence
docs.text:
Start with CODE SPEED, ALL CW MESSAGES CHAINABLE, and WEIGHT; inherited help remains labeled in that reference.

Source check

Selection and conflict handling: uCWKeyerBase.pas. Implementations: uCWKeyerCAT.pas, uCWKeyerWinKey.pas, uCWKeyerYCCC.pas, and uCWKeyerCPU.pas. UI: ui/lcl/uKeyerEditForm.lfm. The factory design (docs/CW_Keyer_Factory_Plan.md) provides historical rationale; its older output descriptions are not proof of current platform support. No on-air keying tests were run for this guide.

docs.title: Send contacts to external loggers
docs.text: TR4W can send contacts to several named external loggers. Each destination has its own queue and delivery state. Network work runs away from the main logging window; saving a contact does not mean the receiving logger has accepted it yet.

docs.title: Configure destinations
docs.text:
1. Open Ctrl+J → External Software → External Logger.
  2. Choose Add..., give the destination a useful name, and select its provider. Enter that provider's connection details.
  3. Select Enabled for destinations that should send new QSOs. Drag an Order cell to change their order. Double-click a row, or right-click and choose Edit..., to edit it.
  4. Save Preferences. Enabled and Order changes apply immediately on Save. A new destination or changed connection details require a restart; check for Restart TR4W to apply in the row.
  5. In a practice log, send one contact and check it in every enabled receiving logger. Compare the call, UTC time, band, mode, and exchange.

Order controls dispatch order, not the order in which independent remote services finish. Changing a destination's name does not redirect its existing backlog to another account.

docs.title: Provider details and limits
docs.text:
Provider Connection details Changes and deletes DXKeeper Receiving TCP host/IP and port Supported; replacement can involve deleting and re-sending the QSO. Check the receiving log after an interrupted replacement. World Radio League API key and a logbook from the retrieved list Supported, with persistent delivery and retry state. Use Create logbook… on the WRL row when you need a new logbook. Club Log Club Log callsign and API token Supported through the bearer-token QSO API. An edit deletes the old remote QSO then creates its replacement; a failure between these steps requires review. No Club Log email/password is needed. QRZ Logbook Logbook callsign and API access key from your QRZ logbook settings. One definition per callsign. An edit deletes the old QRZ entry and inserts its replacement. Review the receiving log if a replacement fails. Cloudlog / Wavelog Server URL, API key, station profile ID New QSOs only. Editing or deleting a previously sent QSO produces a failed delivery row. Correct the remote log manually. ACLog Host/IP and port, default 127.0.0.1:1100. Enable TCP API Enabled in ACLog. New QSOs only. Changes and deletes of sent QSOs fail explicitly. Direct delivery bypasses ACLog contest scoring.

The ACLog radio-control bridge is separate from the ACLog logger. The setup wizard can also configure an external logger.

For Log4OM, use TR4W's standard UDP contact-broadcast settings rather than adding an external-logger provider. New-QSO forwarding is documented in the change history; edit forwarding still needs verification.

docs.title: Check delivery and credentials
docs.text:
Review pending, retrying, uncertain, and failed counts. Enabled means a destination is selected for sending, not that all its contacts have arrived. A persistent queue can resume earlier work after startup, before you log a new QSO. Investigate an uncertain result in the receiving log before retrying it, to avoid duplicates.

Right-click a configured logger row for Open web site when available, or Resend QSOs…. The resend dialog applies to the current contest and that destination. Choose undelivered QSOs or all QSOs. Check the remote log before using All to avoid duplicate work or entries.

Not every remote API supports the same operations. A successful create does not establish that a later edit or delete succeeded. Keep the TR4W log and inspect the receiving log when a delivery fails.

API keys and passwords use the operating system's credential store. Copying the settings file to another computer does not copy those secrets; re-enter credentials there. Resolve a locked or unavailable credential store rather than expecting a plaintext fallback.

Source and review boundary

Reviewed for 5.1.0 against the provider units, registry, queue service, and external-logger grid. Live service behavior requires verification with the intended account and server.

docs.title: Language and internationalization
docs.text:
Internationalization (I18N) is the machinery that lets one TR4W build present its interface in different languages. Translation supplies the actual wording. A language option does not by itself establish that every phrase has been reviewed.

See Available languages and translation status for all language names, command-line testing codes, earlier translation credits, and measured review/empty counts. Italian, French, and the other newly seeded catalogues require review of their machine-generated drafts.

The 5.1.0 update adds machine-drafted help for 15 languages and new interface strings. The reference counts catalogue flags at the release tag. Human review remains necessary before treating a translation as approved.

docs.title: Choose the interface language
docs.text:
Use Language: in Preferences and restart TR4W to load the chosen interface language. The startup selection order is:

  1. An explicit --lang, -l, or --lang= command-line option.
  2. The saved language setting, if this build has that catalogue.
  3. The operating system's language.
  4. Compiled-in English when no usable translation is loaded.

For example, --lang=de requests German for that launch. An unavailable saved language is skipped so the OS language can be considered. An unknown explicit switch is reported by the loader and can result in English rather than silently honoring a different saved preference.

docs.title: What changes and what stays stable
docs.text:
The UI catalogue translates resource strings and form properties: menus, captions, buttons, and messages. Configuration help has its own catalogue. Literal command names used by configuration parsing remain the documented command vocabulary; translate the explanation rather than changing a command such as WSJT-X BROADCAST PORT.

Keep callsigns, park references, protocol fields, and format placeholders intact. A localized display does not change the meaning of an ADIF field or a radio-control command.

docs.title: Embedded catalogues and overrides
docs.text:
The program carries language catalogues in its resources, so routine language selection does not require a separate translated executable. A languages/<code>/tr4w.po file under the application's shipped-data root takes precedence over the embedded catalogue. The loader resolves it through DataFilePath; “beside the executable” is only accurate for layouts where that is the data root. Use a test installation when trying an override, rather than modifying a signed application bundle.

An override can therefore explain why two installations of the same build show different wording. Include any override and the selected language when reporting a translation problem.

docs.title: Unreviewed translations in this preview
docs.text:
Current testing policy differs from the older translator guide

The current resource build includes unreviewed/fuzzy entries for testing by default. It removes their fuzzy markers from the embedded copy so the runtime loader will display them; source .po files retain those review markers. The build option Make-LanguageRes.ps1 -ReviewedOnly excludes fuzzy entries.

Consequently, text appearing in this preview is not proof that a translator has approved it. Older documentation saying that unreviewed strings can never appear is out of date for this snapshot. Missing translations can leave English visible alongside translated text.

docs.title: Help improve a translation
docs.text:
Work on the appropriate .po catalogue: tr4w_<code>.po for the interface, or help_<code>.po for configuration help. Review contesting terms in their actual context—especially dupe, multiplier, exchange, run, S&P, and spot. Preserve formatting placeholders such as %s, %d, and %.2f, including their types and order; they are filled by the program. Menu Alt+letter mnemonics have been removed in 5.0.37; assigned command shortcuts remain. Do not add menu shortcut markers expecting the old behavior. Test translated control text, assigned shortcuts, and layout in the application. Review the text in the application before marking a translation reviewed. See the language and review-status table for the catalogue names and command-line language codes.

For a useful report, include the TR4W version, OS, selected language, window/control, the displayed wording, and a proposed correction. A screenshot helps identify clipped text and ambiguous context. This MkDocs prototype is currently English; application localization does not automatically translate these pages.

docs.title: Supporting documents
docs.text:
• Translator guide (docs/TRANSLATOR_GUIDE.md): translator workflow; read its review-policy claims with the correction above.
  • Translation tools (docs/I18N_TOOLS.md): catalogue maintenance. Its three-letter tool arguments differ from the UI loader's language tags.
  • Language selection implementation (tr4w/src/uUILanguage.pas)
  • Embedded catalogue loader (tr4w/src/ui/lcl/uEmbeddedTranslations.pas)

Language selection and translated layout still require a walkthrough on each target desktop. This page documents source behavior, not a completed translation audit.

docs.title: Multi-station networking
docs.text:
Upgrade the server and all stations together

TR4W 5.1.0 uses protocol 5. Earlier clients and servers cannot join a protocol 5 network. For TR4WServerPy, use a build that explicitly supports protocol 5. A different application build on the same protocol can connect and may show a version notice.

Protocol 5 creates a server database named SERVERLOG.tr4wsrv. Preserve the old SERVERLOG.TRW and the contest databases from every station before upgrading. The server leaves the old file in place and starts with an empty database. Reconnect each station to restore the contacts it originally logged through catch-up.

On macOS, obtain tr4wserver from the matching .dmg or .tar.gz when the Mac will host the network. The .pkg installs the desktop application only. Open the Network window for details about the main-window Network indicator.

TR4W stations connect to TR4WServer to exchange contest activity. This network is separate from a radio's network CAT connection, a DX cluster, and WSJT-X UDP traffic.

docs.title: Set up a practice network
docs.text:
1. Choose the server computer and run a compatible TR4WServer build for the clients being tested.
  2. On each client, select the same contest and set Server, Port, and Password in Ctrl+J → Network. For a remote server that provides a Tailcat address, follow Tailcat setup.
  3. Give every station a distinct letter in This station (the COMPUTER ID setting). The station-status display uses these letters to identify stations.
  4. Make the server's main port and its synchronization port reachable. The conventional main port is 1061; the synchronization port is main port + 1, normally 1062.
  5. Choose Net → Connect. Check the Network and Stations displays, log a practice contact, and confirm that the other clients receive the contact and station state.
  6. Test a disconnect/reconnect and a log mismatch before the event. Preserve each station's test log so you can compare what happened.

Keep each client's database in its own intended location and use the application's network protocol. Do not substitute multiple processes writing one shared SQLite file for TR4W networking.

docs.title: Catch up after a disconnect
docs.text:
TR4W compares contacts by their stored identity. It adds contacts missing from the station after taking a local backup. In the other direction, it sends contacts logged at that station that the server lacks. Contacts received from other stations and imported contacts are excluded from that upload. A different contest blocks catch-up.

If there is work to do, TR4W asks before transferring contacts, unless SERVER AUTO SYNCHRONIZE LOG ON CONNECT is enabled. The upload notice gives the total and breaks out contacts logged while disconnected from contacts the server lacked. If you rebuilt the server, check the resulting contact count after each originating station reconnects.

docs.title: Shared settings
docs.text: Only designated contest options are shared, including certain scoring, multiplier and QTC settings. Preferences can send changes to connected peers on an explicit save. Connecting does not push an entire settings file. Each station keeps its own band, mode, code speed, CW tone, weight and Farnsworth settings. A checksum detects damaged QSO records. Use a trusted network for direct connections or use the encrypted Tailcat tunnel.

docs.title: Tailcat
docs.text:
Tailcat tunnels the contest-log connection between networks. Every client and the server still need protocol 5. A radio, rotator or amplifier uses its own separate remote-control setup.

  1. Obtain the Tailcat address privately from the operator of a compatible Tailcat-enabled server. Treat the address like a password.
  2. Open Preferences → Network, paste the address, and select Use Tailcat. Keep the configured TR4W server port and password. TR4W uses the tunnel in place of the direct server address.
  3. Connect and verify that both live logging and catch-up work. If TR4W reports that the Tailcat library is missing, check the installed package and matching library before retrying.

docs.title: Post scores to HamScore
docs.text:
The HamScore integration sends live score information and can also send QSO contact data to the configured service. It is separate from exporting a Cabrillo entry and does not submit your contest entry to the sponsor.

  1. Open Ctrl+J → Operating → Online Scoring.
  2. Enable Post my score while the contest runs.
  3. Set Service URL, Username, and Password for your service account. An empty username falls back to your configured callsign; an empty password prevents the uploader from starting.
  4. Decide whether to Include contact information. QSO uploads require this setting and a contest marked RTC-capable by TR4W. Turning it off suppresses contact log/edit/delete uploads; score posts remain enabled.
  5. Save the preferences and restart TR4W; this page's settings take effect at startup.
  6. Open Windows → HamScore RTC Status and check the queue and last status. Confirm the result on your scoreboard account before relying on it during a contest.

Normally the worker posts every two minutes. Push Now requests an immediate cycle. Unconfirmed contacts remain queued for retry; explicit server confirmation clears them. A growing queue or repeated error needs attention: check credentials, service URL, connectivity, and whether the service accepts the contest. Both radios use the same uploader.

docs.title: Check scoring URLs
docs.text: The default HamScore URL is https://hamscore.com/postxml/ and the default scoreboard posting URL is https://contestonlinescore.com/post/. TR4W updates a saved old default once and preserves a custom URL. Use Test next to a URL to check its HTTP response. A 200 response confirms reachability and does not verify an actual score upload. Keep Verify the server's certificate enabled for each destination. The global certificate setting controls whether TLS verification can run.

docs.title: Rebuild the remote log
docs.text:
Tools → Re-send Log to HamScore... and the status window's Re-send Log to HamScore... button open the same confirmation dialog:

  • Re-send only uploads the current contacts with their original IDs, without deleting remote contacts. A QSO deleted locally can therefore remain on the server.
  • Delete and re-send deletes the server's log for this contest, then uploads the current contacts. The remote deletion cannot be undone, and the scoreboard can be empty or incomplete until the upload finishes.
  • Cancel leaves the queue unchanged.

Both sending choices request an immediate upload cycle. Confirm the correct contest/account and contact-upload settings before proceeding. Neither choice deletes the local database. Older builds used a different caption and had an incomplete status-window resync action; those instructions no longer describe this source.

A server request for ResyncLog is reported for manual action rather than automatically rebuilding. Do not treat the in-memory upload queue as a backup of the local database. See backups and diagnostic logging for recovery evidence.

Source check

uHamScore.pas worker, configuration and queue helpers; uPrefsForm.lfm Online scoring controls; uHamScoreForm button handlers; MainUnit Tools handler calling both HamScoreResyncFromScratch and SendFullLogToHamScore. No credentials were entered and no score data was posted while preparing this guide.

docs.title: Connect a radio
docs.text:
Check the radio support table for the driver's registered serial/network connections, discovery support, and setup defaults. For a TCI connection, also read TCI connections.

Open Ctrl+J → Hardware → Radios. Choose Add..., or select an existing radio and choose Edit.... The setup wizard can open the editor too. Confirm Name and Radio type before entering connection details.

Serial CATNetwork CAT
  1. Select the appropriate Radio type and open Serial.
  2. Choose the Port used by your radio's CAT interface.
  3. Match Baud rate, Data bits, Parity, and Stop bits to the radio's CAT settings.
  4. Set CAT RTS and CAT DTR according to the interface requirements.
  5. For an Icom radio, verify CI-V address (hex) against the radio's configuration.
  1. Select the appropriate Radio type and open Network.
  2. Enter IP address and IP port for the radio's control service.
  3. If discovery is available for that model, use Discover and select the radio in Found.
  4. Supply User name and Password if required by the radio's network service.
  5. Check the radio's own network-control configuration if the connection fails.

Choose Save and close to keep the configuration, or Cancel to discard the dialog changes.

docs.title: Network radios and software interfaces
docs.text:
• Elecraft K4. Discovery lists each address with its radio name. Choose the address reachable from your station when both Wi-Fi and Ethernet are connected.
  • FLRig. Select FLRig (XML-RPC) as the network radio type and use the FLRig host and port, default 12345. The native driver provides radio control. PTT by CAT is unconfirmed and CW requires a separate keying method.
  • DXLab Commander. Select DXLab Commander to control a radio through that program, default TCP port 52002. CW by CAT is implemented and still needs verification on a real rig. TR4W's Commander-compatible endpoint for WSJT-X runs in the opposite direction.
  • Flex API. The driver checks the link every second and reconnects a link that has been silent for ten seconds.

Verify PTT by CAT and CW on the intended radio before relying on either. TR4W reports when the selected driver is known to lack CAT PTT.

docs.title: Per-radio polling
docs.text: In the newer radio editor, FREQUENCY POLL RATE is under Advanced for each radio. Set it for the selected radio rather than looking for a station-wide value. Check both configured radios after changing profiles or polling settings.

docs.title: Verify the connection
docs.text:
Tune the radio and check that TR4W follows its frequency. Then check a mode change. If either fails, confirm the selected model and transport settings before investigating other integrations.

Symptom First checks Serial radio does not respond Correct CAT port, matching serial parameters, and whether another application owns the port. Network radio does not respond Radio address, control-service port, credentials where required, and network reachability. Discovery finds nothing Discovery support for this model and whether the radio is reachable on the local network; try its known address. Frequency works but CW does not Keying configuration. CAT frequency control and CW output are separate checks.

The form has separate Keyer output port, Keyer RTS line, and Keyer DTR line controls. Configure these for your keying interface; do not assume the CAT connection selects a keying method automatically.

Source check

Control names: tr4w/src/ui/lcl/uRadioEditForm.lfm. This page documents the configuration surface; it does not certify a particular radio/OS combination. The older TCP/IP wiki guide has additional model context.

docs.title: Icom network recovery and band selection
docs.text:
After a rejected login, check the credentials in the radio configuration and save the correction. Saving reapplies the configuration to a running radio. Authentication failures are retried with a 60-second delay; repeated resets are not a substitute for waiting for recovery. A successful operational connection clears the prior authentication condition. If updates still do not resume, use Reset Radio Ports below.

Icom session renewal and keepalives now maintain the LAN connection. Band-up/down uses the radio's reported transmit bands where supported; a radio that cannot provide a band plan retains its fallback stepping behavior.

The current band model includes 1.25 m (222 MHz), 33 cm (902 MHz), and 23 cm (1296 MHz). Earlier builds could classify these as 70 cm, affecting logging, dupe checks, and scoring. Verify the band shown before logging; do not assume upgrading repairs contacts already stored under the wrong band. Compare suspect contacts with your station records before correcting or exporting them.

docs.title: Reset Radio Ports
docs.text:
Use Reset Radio Ports when CAT frequency/mode updates have stopped after a USB interruption, a radio restart, or a lost network connection and the connection has not recovered. First check the radio power, cable or network, and configured device/address. A reset cannot fix a wrong serial device, baud rate, network address, or credentials.

Stop transmitting before resetting. The action reinitializes both the active and inactive radio interfaces: it stops old polling, disconnects, frees and recreates the radio objects, and reconnects using their configuration. It is not limited to serial ports despite its name.

Afterward, turn each radio's tuning knob and check that its panel follows; verify band, mode, and CW/PTT operation before resuming. If it still fails, inspect the diagnostic log rather than repeatedly resetting. This action does not restore a log, reset the contest, or replace the separate WinKey configuration/reopen action.

Source: MainUnit.ResetRadioPorts calls CheckAndInitializePorts_ForThisRadio for both radios; SetUpRadioInterface owns interface teardown and recreation.

docs.title: SO2R: one operator, two radios
docs.text: SO2R lets you run on one radio while searching for another contact on the other. TR4W distinguishes the active radio, whose operating context you are using, from the inactive radio. Two radio windows alone do not configure audio, PTT, or CW routing.

docs.title: Commission the station
docs.text:
1. Configure and test each radio connection separately. Open both radio panels and check frequency, mode, and active-radio indication.
  2. Configure the intended CW keyer and station switching hardware. Verify which radio is keyed and which audio you hear for each selection. A successful CAT connection does not establish correct transmit routing.
  3. Open Ctrl+J → Operating → Two Radio Mode and enable Two radio mode. The earlier SO2R tips also recommend ALT-D BUFFER ENABLE and TUNE ALT-D ENABLE for an inactive-radio search workflow; configure these to suit your operation.
  4. Test Alt+R to swap radios. Confirm the active highlight and logging band/mode, then swap back.
  5. Rehearse a complete contact on each radio in a practice log before adding automation.

docs.title: Use the inactive radio
docs.text:
Alt+D invokes dupe checking on the inactive radio. Use it to investigate a call while retaining the running-radio context. The Alt-D buffer and tuning option support bringing spotted calls into this workflow. Check the displayed radio and contact before completing the QSO; Alt+R is the explicit swap action.

For a band map focused on the search radio, review SO2R DISPLAY, disable ALL BANDS if appropriate, and configure QSY INACTIVE RADIO. See band map operation for the actual filters and tuning behavior. Verify a spot selection tunes the intended radio before using it during a run.

docs.title: Add message automation gradually
docs.text:
Program ordinary CQ and exchange messages first, then add inactive-radio sending or radio-swap commands through the message editor. The earlier wiki warns that combining inactive-radio transmission with a focus switch while entering the running radio's exchange can associate that contact with the other radio. Finish or deliberately preserve the current contact before changing context.

Practice stopping messages with Esc, recovering from a mistaken swap, and checking the logged band/mode. The old recommendation to use WinKey is an operating suggestion, not a requirement that every SO2R installation use that hardware: the current application also has CAT and YCCC sending paths. Their availability and routing depend on the configured hardware and driver.

Source check

Baseline: wiki SO2R-Tips.md. Current checks: MainUnit handlers for menu_alt_dupecheck and menu_alt_tooglerigs, uAccelerators (Alt+D/Alt+R), the current command reference, radio-panel active tint, and the CW adapters. Hardware timing, interlocks, and a complete two-radio contest remain bench-review tasks.

docs.title: TCI connections
docs.text:
TCI can connect TR4W to a software-defined radio application, or let other software control a radio already connected to TR4W. Choose the direction you need before configuring ports.

Your goal TR4W's role Configure here Control a TCI-capable radio application from TR4W TCI client / native radio driver Radio configuration Let another program control TR4W's connected radio TCI server Preferences, TCI Server

These are separate connections. Neither one supplies a complete audio setup.

docs.title: Connect TR4W to a TCI radio application
docs.text:
1. Enable the TCI service in the radio application and note its address and port.
  2. In TR4W's radio configuration, select TCI (ExpertSDR / Thetis / AetherSDR).
  3. Enter the radio application's address and port under Network. The registration seeds port 50001; use the actual service port if different.
  4. Save the radio configuration and check frequency and mode updates before testing transmit functions.

This is a native TR4W driver, registered under ID TCI, with a network connection and no discovery support. The older Expert TCI (HamLib bridge) is a separate placeholder whose backend is described as unavailable in the shipped Hamlib build; choosing it does not select the native driver.

docs.title: Let another application connect to TR4W
docs.text:
1. Establish and verify the radio's normal connection to TR4W first.
  2. Open Ctrl+J → TCI Server and select Enable the TCI server.
  3. Set Port: to an unused listening port and apply the settings.
  4. In the client application, select its TCI connection and use TR4W's address and the same port.
  5. Check the intended receiver: TR4W maps Radio 1 to trx 0 and Radio 2 to trx 1.
  6. Verify frequency and mode control before testing PTT. Set Stop transmitting after: to the transmit limit appropriate for your test.

By default, the server listens on the local computer (127.0.0.1). Also listen on the network (other computers can connect) changes that scope. The form warns that this is an unauthenticated control socket: a reachable client can move the VFO and key the transmitter. Leave network listening off when all clients run locally.

docs.title: What the server does not provide
docs.text: The server does not emit audio or IQ streams; clients still need their own audio path. Its handlers also identify cw_msg and CW-speed requests as unimplemented in this snapshot. Do not infer server support from capabilities of the separate native TCI radio driver.

docs.title: TCI and WSJT-X
docs.text:
WSJT-X UDP integration carries decoded-call, highlight, and logged-QSO information. TCI concerns a radio-control connection. Configuring one does not automatically configure the other. Confirm which radio-control interfaces your particular client build actually offers.

Evidence and review status

Native registration: radioFactory/uRadioTCI.pas. Bridge limitation: radioFactory/uRadioHamLibOnly.pas. Server behavior and limits: uTCIServer.pas. Controls: ui/lcl/uPrefsForm.lfm. This is source-checked documentation; no TCI client/server bench test was performed for this page.

docs.title: Connect WSJT-X
docs.text:
WSJT-X performs the digital-mode work. TR4W receives its UDP messages to support contest logging and callsign highlighting.

You can also configure WSJT-X from Tools → Setup Wizard during station setup.

docs.title: Match the UDP connection
docs.text:
In a practice contest, press Ctrl+J and select External Software → WSJT-X.

  1. Check Exchange data with WSJT-X and note the Broadcast port. The default is 2237.
  2. In WSJT-X's Settings → Reporting, set the UDP server destination and port. For both apps on one computer, the destination is typically 127.0.0.1. Leave Multicast group blank in TR4W.
  3. For a shared multicast setup, match the group and port in both apps and select the outgoing interface in WSJT-X.
  4. For highlighting, check Send callsign highlighting to WSJT-X in TR4W and Accept UDP requests in WSJT-X.
  5. Save Preferences. Restart TR4W after enabling WSJT-X or changing the broadcast port.

docs.title: Verify both directions
docs.text:
Confirm that decoded calls receive the expected highlighting. Then, when you complete and confirm a QSO in WSJT-X, check that it appears once in TR4W with the expected call, band, mode, and exchange.

TR4W can fill a missing state from the received grid when the lookup gives a unique answer. If the grid spans more than one state, it shows the candidates for you to check. Live WSJT-X records use the open TR4W contest.

If you see this Check this No received activity Matching port, destination/group, selected network interface, and local firewall rules. Contacts arrive but no highlights Accept UDP requests in WSJT-X and Send Highlights in TR4W. Duplicate logged contacts Whether both WSJT-X and another forwarding application are sending the same QSO to TR4W.

docs.title: Radio control is a separate connection
docs.text: First verify TR4W's radio connection. On the WSJT-X Preferences page shown above, select Let WSJT-X control the radio, save, and restart TR4W. Select DX Lab Suite Commander as the rig in WSJT-X and point it at TR4W's Commander-compatible TCP service, default port 52002. Test frequency and mode changes with the intended rig.

docs.title: Receive N1MM-style log messages
docs.text:
On the WSJT-X Preferences page shown above, select Accept QSOs from JTDX and JTAlert (N1MM log listener) for a sender configured to forward N1MM Logger+ Log messages. The listener is off by default. TR4W listens on UDP 2333 and TCP 52001. Address the N1MM log listener binds to defaults to 127.0.0.1 for senders on the same computer. To receive from another computer, set the listener to this station's LAN address and allow only trusted senders to reach it. Both settings apply when saved. Any sender that can reach the listener can add records to the open contest log.

Choose one forwarding path per sender. A resent contact can be logged and flagged as a dupe. This listener receives contact records and does not provide WSJT-X highlighting or CAT control.

WSJT-X setting names and defaults

The full command reference includes scope, value constraints, and source initial values. TCI connections explains the separate radio-control path; external loggers explains forwarding contacts beyond TR4W.

Evidence and review status

Adapted from the WSJT-X integration wiki page, with setting names and defaults checked against uSettingsModel.pas. UDP and highlighting behavior still need an operator test with the intended WSJT-X version. The wiki's older instruction to edit tr4w.ini has deliberately not been carried forward.

docs.title: SQLite integrity and durability
docs.text: TR4W uses a SQLite database as the contest log. Protection comes from several checks at different stages, not from a single “database is safe” flag.

docs.title: Before accepting contacts
docs.text:
The database layer checks file identity and schema version. A foreign database or a schema newer than the program understands is refused rather than treated as a compatible log.

Before upgrading an older schema, the log store requests and verifies a snapshot. A failed backup stops the upgrade before changes to the original database. The 5.1.0 station log uses schema 13. The protocol 5 server store has its own format and file extension.

On opening the contest store, TR4W checks database integrity and then checks whether it can write. An integrity failure prevents normal logging and reports the problem. If another process locks the log, startup offers Retry, Open read-only (no logging), or Quit TR4W. Read-only mode permits viewing and export but cannot save QSOs. Release the other process's lock and retry when you need to log; opening read-only does not repair a damaged database. Opening a file successfully is not treated as proof that a later QSO can be saved.

Check What it detects Application identity and schema version Wrong file type or unsupported schema SQLite integrity_check Structural database problems; success requires the result ok SQLite foreign_key_check Broken relationships between records Writability probe A database that opens but cannot accept writes

The full integrity check runs on open; it is not a full database scan after every QSO.

docs.title: When saving a contact
docs.text:
The append path starts with a failure result and returns success only after the repository commit succeeds. This makes “saved” depend on persistence rather than merely placing a row on screen.

Linked county-line, multi-park, and rover rows are committed as a batch. A refused save keeps the entry in the operating window and suppresses outbound delivery. When a full disk leaves the log read-only, see resume after a full disk.

The write connection requests synchronous = FULL and write-ahead logging (journal_mode = WAL). It reads back the actual journal mode and foreign-key enforcement state. Foreign-key enforcement is required. WAL is requested rather than assumed; the connection records the mode SQLite actually supplies.

In WAL mode, recent committed data can reside in a companion -wal file. The main .db file alone is therefore not necessarily a complete live copy of the contest.

docs.title: When making a backup
docs.text:
The backup path creates a consistent SQLite snapshot, including committed data still in the WAL. It writes to a staged .new file, opens that snapshot on a separate read-only connection, checks it, then publishes it by rename. An existing destination is retained as .bak during replacement.

Verification is read-only so it does not change the bytes being checked. Failure cases report the surviving filenames, including a verified .new file when publication fails. See Back up your log for the operating procedure.

The periodic worker snapshots through its own read-only connection and coalesces requests. Backups required before upgrading, clearing, or bulk correcting station facts complete before the corresponding write proceeds.

docs.title: What these protections cannot prove
docs.text:
A successful integrity check does not validate callsigns, received exchanges, the contest category, or the sponsor's scoring rules. Durable commits also depend on the operating system and storage device honoring writes. No database setting eliminates disk loss, accidental deletion, or the need for a separate backup.

If TR4W reports an integrity or write failure, preserve the database and its companion files, retain the diagnostic log, and work from a separate recovery copy. Do not delete a WAL file as a troubleshooting shortcut.

docs.title: Supporting evidence
docs.text:

These are implementation-backed explanations for the documented snapshot, not a report of a power-loss or hardware-failure test performed for this guide.

docs.title: How the parts work together
docs.text:
TR4W connects several sources of information to one contest: your entries, radio state, cluster spots, and messages from other applications. Each has a different role.

Part What it contributes What it does not establish Radio connection Frequency, mode, and supported control operations That a contact was completed or saved CW sending path Delivers text or keying through the selected method That the other operator received it DX cluster and band map Candidate stations and operating frequencies That a spotted call or exchange is correct Contest rules and multiplier state Interpret exchanges and track worked multipliers The sponsor's final adjudicated score SQLite contest log Stores contacts and contest-associated data An independent backup on another device Export and external loggers Deliver contact data to another format or application That a sponsor has accepted a submission

docs.title: From a contact to a saved record
docs.text:
The entry and contest logic construct a contact record. The log store sends it through the repository to SQLite. A boundary or multi-park entry commits all of its rows together. Only after a successful commit does TR4W publish the contact to the multi-op link, external loggers, and UDP destinations. The record retains the applicable station facts and contest X-QSO decision for display and export.

On a multi-op network, the server keeps a separate SQLite log of the fields shared by protocol 5. Each client owns its contest database. On reconnect, contacts are compared by identity and the client adds missing rows in a transaction. See multi-station networking for upgrade and catch-up behavior.

This division is useful when diagnosing a problem. A radio can follow frequency correctly while a keyer is misconfigured. A structurally sound database can contain a mistyped exchange. A correct export can still have the wrong submission category.

docs.title: From a cluster line to an operating decision
docs.text: A cluster connection receives text; spot parsing extracts fields such as call and frequency. Spot and contest logic determine what to display and whether a station may be a new multiplier or a dupe. The band-map view filters and paints that data. Selecting a spot can tune a radio; it does not log a completed QSO.

Evidence

This overview summarizes the source snapshot used throughout the guide: uLogStore.pas, uLogRepository.pas, domain/uLogDatabase.pas, uDXClusterClient.pas, uTelnet.pas, uSpots.pas, and the LCL display forms. The following pages link the supporting implementation and test documents.

docs.title: Test methodology
docs.text: TR4W uses several kinds of checks because one passing suite cannot establish that every contest, radio, desktop, and export works correctly.

docs.title: The layers
docs.text: Layer What it exercises Representative evidence Focused unit tests Parsers, mappings, state transitions, and contest calculations uTestMults, uTestCWKeyer, uTestCWFraming, uTestDXClusterClient Real SQLite tests Schema, identity, pragmas, writability, snapshots, and persistence uTestLogDatabase, uTestLogRepository Injected failure tests Backup failures that are difficult to reproduce on demand uTestLogBackup Golden export corpus A known contest database produces expected ADIF and Cabrillo tr4w/test/corpus/README.md UI checks Control population, layout, and interaction in a running build tr4w/test/ui/ Radio bench and operator tests Actual transport, keying, timing, and contest workflow Bench plans and status documents in docs/

docs.title: Real data and independent expectations
docs.text:
The export corpus uses SQLite contest logs as input and retained D7-produced ADIF/Cabrillo files as expected output. Keeping those expected files independent matters: regenerating them from the implementation under test could preserve a new defect as the new expectation.

Legacy binary-log conversion is exercised by separate unit fixtures. The old Python export-verifier README describes an earlier .TRW-based workflow; it should not be mistaken for the current corpus input contract.

docs.title: Deliberately testing failure
docs.text:
Database tests create real temporary SQLite databases. Backup tests combine real files and real valid snapshots with injected failures, including corrupt staged output, snapshot exceptions, and failed publication. They check which files survive and the report given to the operator.

This is stronger evidence for those paths than testing only that the normal backup creates a file. It is still not a substitute for testing real storage loss or power interruption.

docs.title: How to read a test result
docs.text:
A useful result identifies the source revision, platform/toolchain, suite or corpus, and pass/fail/skip outcome. A skipped hardware or platform check is not a pass. An accepted export difference should be documented rather than silently changing the expected output.

This documentation update ran the documentation generator and strict MkDocs build, not the application test suites. The existence of a test in the repository is evidence of intended coverage, not evidence that it passed today.

docs.title: Recent connection and interface evidence
docs.text:
The September 27 development record reports a 7 hour 52 minute LAN soak with an IC-7760 and IC-9700: one login per radio, no CI-V data timeouts, and clean shutdown. This is evidence for those radios and that tested setup, not certification of every supported model or platform.

New focused tests cover radio-band mapping, Icom teardown ownership, retry delays, status-versus-notice lifetime, menu shortcuts, and focused editing keys. Release packaging also checks that separate debug symbols match the binaries shipped. A matching symbol file improves crash diagnosis; it does not prove a contest workflow works.

These are recorded development results and source coverage reviewed for this guide. No application, installer, or hardware test was rerun during the September 29 documentation update.
